entry.title: New E-learning: SAP S/4HANA Finance for Cash Management and Treasury & Risk Management
entry.content:
In today’s fast-paced business landscape, organizations are under growing pressure to optimize working capital, mitigate financial risks, and maintain greater visibility over cash flows. Disconnected data sources, manual processes, and limited real-time insights can hinder effective cash utilization, slow decision-making, and increase the risk of missed opportunities.

To overcome these challenges, businesses need an integrated solution that provides a holistic view of their financial position and supports proactive cash and risk management. Discover how SAP S/4HANA Finance for Cash Management and Treasury Risk Management helps organizations enhance liquidity planning, improve financial visibility, and strengthen risk controls in this comprehensive 2.5-hour e-learning course.

What You'll Learn

The course introduces the core capabilities of SAP S/4HANA Finance for Cash Management and Treasury and Risk Management and explains how organizations can improve cash visibility, liquidity planning, and financial risk management through an integrated treasury solution. Learners will explore key functionalities such as bank account management, bank statement processing, liquidity management, and the end-to-end lifecycle of financial transactions and risk management.

The course also covers extended treasury capabilities, including situation handling, integration scenarios, payment reason determination, intercompany transaction mirroring, benchmark reform compliance, hedge accounting and management, and treasury analytics. In addition, participants will gain an understanding of how these capabilities help organizations streamline treasury operations, reduce cash management costs, strengthen risk controls, and support more informed financial decision-making.

Ready to Get Started?

Take the next step in your learning journey by enrolling in the Optimizing Working Capital with SAP S/4HANA Finance: Cash Management and Treasury & Risk Management e-learning course.

entry.title: Announcing SAP Pay, Powered by Tereina
entry.content:
SAP Pay was Introduced with the core vision during SAP Connect event on October 6, 2026 

What is SAP Pay?

SAP Pay is the out-of-the-box B2B payments solution embedded in SAP Cloud ERP and provided by Tereina, an SAP entity dedicated to providing payment services, with OFAC and KYC/AML screening applied to every transaction. This gives SAP Cloud ERP customers a built-in way to automate payment execution across traditional and digital currency rails, with no separate implementation project, bank testing, or manual file uploads. Because SAP Pay runs natively inside the ERP environment, finance teams can initiate and manage payments without leaving their existing SAP workflow.

Access every payment rail—traditional and digital—through a single connection, with payment automation, reconciliation, and a unified know-your-customer process that:

  • Supports ACH, EFT, wire, check, and stablecoin payments like USD Coin (USDC).
  • Auto-reconciles every payment to its originating purchase order (PO) or invoice.
  • Covers 89 global corridors—no per-country bank setup required.
  • Autonomously initiates and executes payments using AI agents.

SAP Pay powered by Tereina

Reduce payment costs and drive payment automation with embedded, agentic B2B payments across traditional and digital currency rails.


Key features

Multi-rail payment support—your payment, your option

SAP Pay supports fiat and digital currencies and many payment types. This includes real-time payments, alongside USDC stablecoin payments with native integration to Circle, and an intelligent routing to the optimal rail for each transaction across 40+ currencies—all from a single platform.

Natively embedded in SAP S/4HANA

SAP Pay ships as an out-of-the-box capability inside SAP Cloud ERP, with secure bank communication handled via SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity. There’s no implementation project, no new vendor contract, and no custom code—customers activate it inside existing SAP workflow and it runs.

Agentic payment execution

SAP Pay embeds payment execution into SAP now, the foundational step toward agentic payments. The AI agents that already support your finance team through Joule will soon trigger and execute payments, too, closing decision to execution in one flow.

References

SAP Pay
Tereina
SAP Help Documentation 
Security Guide & Setup Process
SAP Store - SAP Pay

 

Watch Demo - SAP Pay Stablecoin Payments

End-to-end demo of a stablecoin payment in SAP Cloud ERP The demo covers the payment of an open supplier invoice with SAP Pay as house bank: creation in the payment run, status tracking in the Payment Monitor, the transaction in the Tereina portal in USDC and USD, the on-chain transfer in the Circle wallet, the USDC wallet in SAP Short-Term Cash Positioning, and the end-of-day CAMT053 bank statement for posting. Payments are initiated, approved and reconciled in the standard SAP workflow, treasury sees the balance in its normal cash view, and settlement takes minutes instead of days.

FAQ

Is SAP Pay replacing SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity?

No, SAP Pay is using SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity for secure bank communication. SAP Pay provides customers another option to facilitate payments in addition to connecting to banks and payment service providers directly via SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity.

entry.title: Your Pipeline Doesn't Care Where It Starts. Your API Should.
entry.content:
What We Mean by "Linear Asset Data"

 
Before we get into what's new, let's make sure we're talking about the same thing.
Most assets in a plant maintenance system are point assets. A pump. A valve. A motor. They exist at a location, but they don't extend over a distance. You don't ask "which part of the motor?" — it's just the motor.
 
Linear assets are different. A road, a railway track, a pipeline, a conveyor belt, a power line — these assets have length, and everything interesting about them happens at a specific position along that length. The crack in the road surface is at kilometre 7.3. The pipe section with reduced wall thickness runs from 52.1 to 54.6 metres. The speed restriction applies from chainage 1,200 to chainage 1,850.
SAP calls this position information Linear Asset Management data — or LAM data. It typically consists of a start point, an end point, a length (calculated automatically), a unit of measure, and optionally markers and offsets for localised reference systems.
For years, SAP has stored this data beautifully. What it hasn't done — until now — is made it fully available through APIs that integration developers can actually work with.

Three Things That Got Delivered

The 2025 FPS02 release covers three distinct but related capabilities. Think of them as three layers of the same onion.

Layer 1: Position Data on Business Objects

This is the foundational layer. The question it answers is: when you create or manage a business object in SAP — a work order, a notification, a measuring point — can you also set and read its linear position?
The answer is now yes, across ten different APIs.
Let's walk through them, because the breadth here is genuinely impressive.
Equipment and Functional Locations — the master data layer. When you create a piece of linear equipment (say, a section of pipeline registered as an Equipment record), you can now include its linear position data in the same request. One API call, equipment and position created together. For Functional Locations, you get even more flexibility: add position data at creation or add it to an existing record later. Neither object automatically inherits position from its parent in the hierarchy — you set it explicitly, which keeps things clean.
Maintenance Plans and Maintenance Items — the preventive maintenance layer. A maintenance item now carries position data at two levels. At the item header, you get one position record for the overall scope. In the object list — the list of individual objects that the maintenance plan covers — each object can carry multiple position records. Multiple. As in: one object list entry for a pipeline section, with three separate position ranges representing the non-contiguous segments that need the same work done. This is a really practical capability for long infrastructure assets where work doesn't always happen in tidy continuous stretches.
Task Lists — the template layer. Position data is now supported at the task list header level, for both Equipment-based and Functional Location-based task lists. Worth noting: this doesn't carry over automatically from the assigned equipment or location — you set it on the task list itself.
Maintenance Orders — this one is probably the most exciting for execution teams. Three scopes, all covered:
  • The order header gets one position record for the overall work location.
  • Each operation within the order gets its own position record. So if your order has five operations, each one can say "I'm working on this specific stretch." Incredibly useful for multi-crew work on long assets.
  • The object list, just like in the maintenance plan, supports multiple segments per object.
Order Confirmations — when a technician confirms work done, the confirmation now carries position data too. The linear context travels all the way from planning into execution records.
Maintenance Notifications — position data at both the notification header and the notification item level. One design quirk worth knowing: the create and read paths use a navigation property on the notification or item entity, while updates go directly to the linear data record using its own key. It's a small distinction but it matters when you're building an integration.
Measuring Points and Measurement Documents — these use OData V4 (the others above are OData V2), and they bring position data to the measurement layer. Your pressure sensor is at kilometre 12.5. Your measurement document records not just the reading but where on the asset that reading was taken. One quirk here: a locked measuring point returns a 423 Locked response when you try to modify its linear data, rather than the 405 Method Not Allowed you'd get elsewhere. Small thing, but worth knowing before you're debugging at 11pm.

Layer 2: Dynamic Characteristics — What the Asset Is Made Of at Each Point

Knowing where an asset is only tells you half the story. The other half is what it's like at any given position.
Imagine a 50-kilometre road. It's classified in SAP with a class called "Road Properties," which has characteristics like Pavement Type, Number of Lanes, and Speed Limit. But these don't have a single value for the whole road — they change along the way. Pavement type might be concrete from kilometre 0 to 5, asphalt from 5 to 12, concrete again from 12 to 20, and so on.
 
In SAP, this is modelled through the classification system. You assign a class to the asset, the class has characteristics, and each characteristic has values. What was missing was the ability to say where each value applies.
 
That's exactly what the new dynamic characteristic assignment capability delivers. Through both the Equipment API and the Functional Location API, you can now:
  • Assign a position range to any characteristic value (e.g., "Pavement Type = Concrete" applies from 0 to 5 km)
  • Assign multiple non-contiguous ranges to the same value (because that concrete section might come back at km 12)
  • Read all the characteristic-position assignments for an asset in one go
  • Update them as conditions change
  • Delete ones that are no longer valid
It's the missing link between SAP's classification system and the spatial dimension of a linear asset. Once this data is in place, you have everything you need for the third layer.

Layer 3: Dynamic Segmentation — Asking the Asset a Question

Here's where it gets genuinely clever.
 
Say you've got all your characteristic data assigned to position ranges. Now a planner asks: "Show me every segment between chainage 4.8 and 15.0, and tell me what characteristics apply to each one."
This isn't a trivial question. Characteristic values might overlap, have gaps, start and end at different points. Computing the resulting segments manually is exactly the kind of thing no human should have to do in a spreadsheet.
 
The GetLinearSegments function — available on both the Equipment and Functional Location APIs — does this computation for you. You pass in the asset identifier, a start point, end point, and unit of measure, and you get back a list of segments. Each segment is a continuous interval where all the characteristic values are uniform. Every segment tells you what characteristics apply within it.
The Equipment version needs a validity date (Equipment records in SAP are time-versioned). The Functional Location version doesn't need one. If you don't specify a range at all, you get back the full picture for the entire asset.
 
Think about what this unlocks. You can feed a GIS map with dynamically computed segments, colour-coded by condition. You can calculate "how many kilometres of our network have coating type X" without anyone manually counting. You can scope a maintenance order by querying which segments fall below a condition threshold. You can sync SAP's linear characteristic data with any external system that works in segment-based geometry.This is the kind of capability that turns SAP from a data store into an active participant in an asset intelligence platform.

What This Looks Like in Practice

Let's bring it back to the pipeline manager from the beginning of this post.
 
With these APIs, here's what's now possible:
 
A GIS team maintains a spatial data platform that shows the pipeline on a map. Whenever a new maintenance order is created in SAP with a linear position, the GIS system is notified and updates its map layer automatically. No manual data entry. No batch exports.
A mobile inspection app used by field engineers displays the precise section of pipeline they've been assigned. It reads the linear position from the work order operation. When the engineer confirms the inspection, the confirmation is written back with the position intact.
 
A quarterly analytics run calculates the total length of pipeline sections categorised by pipe age and coating condition — by calling GetLinearSegments across the relevant asset population and aggregating the results. What used to take days of manual reporting now runs in minutes.
None of this was straightforward to build before. Now it is.

A Few Things Worth Knowing Before You Start

Consistency is your friend. Across all ten APIs, the update pattern is the same: patch the LinearAssetManagementData entity directly using a type code and a system-assigned key. Once you understand this pattern for one API, it transfers to all the others.
Multiple segments are your friend too. Wherever multiple segments per object are supported — Maintenance Plan Object Lists, Maintenance Order Object Lists — lean into this. It's there because real infrastructure assets don't behave neatly, and neither should your data model.
 
Watch the lock behavior. Some APIs return 423 Locked when you try to write to linear data on a locked object. Others return 405 Method Not Allowed. The Measuring Point API is an example of the former. If your integration does anything with locked objects, test this path explicitly.
 
OData V4 vs V2 matters for the update pattern. The OData V2 APIs use a direct PATCH to the linear data entity and return 204. The OData V4 APIs (Measuring Point, Measurement Document, Task List) use a navigation-based PATCH on the parent entity and return 200 with a response body. Different response handling, so worth accounting for in your client code.
 
Linear data doesn't flow automatically — yet. This one will save you a debugging session, so pay attention. When you create a business object that references a linear asset — a work order for a linear equipment, a notification on a functional location, a task list assigned to a linear object — the system does not currently pull through the linear position data from the referenced asset automatically. No inheritance. No defaulting. No propagation.
This is being worked on. The backend logic for determining and defaulting linear data from parent objects is on the roadmap, but it isn't in this release. Until it is, the rule is simple: if you want linear data on a business object, include it explicitly in your payload. Don't rely on it arriving automatically from the referenced equipment or functional location. Be explicit, be deliberate, and you'll be fine.

The Bigger Picture

It would be easy to look at this release as "a bunch of API enhancements" and move on. But I'd encourage you to see it for what it is: the completion of a capability that SAP has been building for years.
 
The linear asset data model in SAP is rich, well-thought-out, and genuinely useful for infrastructure industries. The classification system for dynamic characteristics is powerful. The segmentation logic is sophisticated. All of that has been in the product for a long time.
 
What's changed is that all of it is now open. Accessible. Integratable. Your GIS, your mobile app, your digital twin, your analytics platform — they can all participate in the linear asset lifecycle now, not just observe it from the outside.
For anyone working with infrastructure assets in SAP — roads, railways, pipelines, utilities — this is a meaningful moment. The data that lives in your SAP system about where things are and what they're made of is now available to every tool in your ecosystem.
 
That's worth getting excited about.
Questions? Drop them in the SAP Community. The PM-LAM team is active there and always up for a conversation about how these capabilities can work for your specific scenario.

entry.title: SNP's Experience with SAP's Max Success Plan
entry.content:
When external perspectives move transformation projects forward

Complex transformation programs regularly reach a point where decisions stall and discussions go in circles. This is exactly what SNP experienced during the modernization of its own SAP landscape. In a conversation, Matthias Schirner, Manager Global IT Business Applications at SNP, explains how the Max Success Plan from SAP helped resolve stalled topics and drive the transformation program forward.

Watch the video interview with Matthias Schirner 

The starting point: ambitious, complex, and blocked in places

With more than 1,700 employees at 34 locations across 22 countries, SNP is one of the leading providers of AI-powered software for SAP transformations and data management. Companies like BMW, Pfizer, and E.ON rely on SNP when implementing complex SAP transformations efficiently and securely.

But even companies with deep transformation expertise face demanding challenges when modernizing their own IT landscape. Four years ago, SNP migrated its SAP system landscape with RISE with SAP to SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition on Microsoft Azure, laying the foundation early for a future-proof cloud strategy. In recent years, this transformation has been consistently driven forward: SAP SuccessFactors for global HR management and SAP Concur for travel and expense management were successfully introduced and rolled out globally. SNP also relies on SAP Business Data Cloud as its central data and analytics platform.

SNP continues to advance the modernization of its SAP landscape. Following the successful move to SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition, the next step in ERP evolution is SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

During the program, it became apparent that certain topics were not progressing as planned. Discussions repeated themselves over months without leading to viable decisions.

Learn more about the Max Success Plan

How the Max Success Plan engagement came about

According to Matthias Schirner, the engagement arose directly from the project situation: "It started in a meeting with SAP where we were talking about the status of our transformation program. We came to the conclusion that it would be best to initiate a workshop to talk about specific challenges and clarify how SAP can help us overcome them."

Together, the teams identified the key challenges and prioritized the most important areas for action. From this developed a tailored service engagement specifically designed to address SNP's requirements.

What the Max Success Plan concretely changed

New perspectives on existing challenges

"The main benefit is that we changed the perspective on our challenges," says Matthias Schirner. The external view — combined with SAP's product and architecture expertise — helped reassess stalled situations and develop clear paths forward.

In long-term transformation programs, teams often develop a fixed view of their challenges over months. An external perspective can help identify new approaches and get decisions moving again.

From endless discussions to clear decisions

"Never-ending discussions, a never-ending series of meetings on the same topic — we were able to stop them and convert them into decisions. Clear decisions. And with that, we ensure that we keep moving forward with our implementation."

For SNP, the value lay not only in additional consulting, but above all in restoring the ability to make decisions within the project. That created the foundation to continue the transformation program with confidence.

Fast impact

Schirner highlights how quickly the engagement delivered results: "It was fantastic to see how quickly this service engagement brought value and quality into our project."

Topics that had been discussed for months were moved into solution-oriented implementation together with the SAP experts in a short time.

Why the Max Success Plan is relevant right now

For SNP, the significance of the project extends beyond the current transformation. "We're talking about AI, about Autonomous Enterprise, about agents," says Schirner. "For us, it's important to build the right foundation for all of that."

Many SAP customers find themselves in a similar situation today. The pace of innovation is continuously increasing. Those who modernize their SAP landscape now are simultaneously creating the prerequisites to leverage future innovations such as AI agents and intelligent automation.

This is where the Max Success Plan comes in. As SAP's most comprehensive service offering, it supports companies in strategically managing complex transformation programs. The three-tier model introduced in March 2026 — Foundational, Advanced, and Max — includes dedicated Success Plan Managers, cross-solution process optimization, customer-specific prototype development, and premium support with response times of up to 15 minutes for highest-priority issues. Or as Matthias Schirner puts it:

"Getting guidance from the SAP experts is the key to our foundation for building the company of the future."

What other SAP customers can take away

SNP's experience reflects a pattern familiar to many transformation programs:

  • Complex projects benefit from different perspectives. Even companies with extensive transformation experience can benefit from the product and architecture expertise of the software vendor.
  • Tailored support creates the greatest value. What made the difference was not a standard program, but a service engagement specifically designed around the concrete challenges at hand.
  • Decision-making capability is a key success factor. When discussions produce no results over a longer period, delays affect project progress, motivation, and planning reliability.
  • Future readiness starts today. Those who want to leverage innovations like AI agents or Autonomous Enterprise are already creating the necessary prerequisites during transformation.
 

See below the offical customer story from SNP.

Conclusion

SNP's experience shows that even companies with deep transformation expertise can benefit from close collaboration with SAP. The Max Success Plan helped the company resolve stalled topics, accelerate decisions, and drive the transformation program forward.

entry.title: SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA – Getting started with Base AI-assisted Features in 2025 FPS2
entry.content:
*** Relevant to SAP S/4HANA release 2025 FPS02 and higher ***

Latest Updates: Business Function activation step has been removed as we have updated advice that this will be done for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition customers - as part of new install, upgrade, conversion, and lift&shift. If you are a RISE customer and interested in using Hybrid AI, please reach out to your SAP contacts.

With SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition release 2025 FPS02, SAP has released 4 new base AI-assisted features to uplift your SAP Fiori user experience.  Importantly, because these features are classed as base AI they are provided for unlimited usage by your users at for you as a customer + these features do NOT require Joule or Joule Work.

This means, you can use them to…

  • Try out some SAP Business AI
  • Upskill on AI activation
  • Get your users working the AI way

…with features embedded directly in your SAP S/4HANA system.

Worth knowing: These features were introduced first to SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud and are now widely used in Public Cloud customer production environments. With release 2025 FPS02 they have been cross-ported to Private Cloud.

The 4 AI-assisted features are:

  • AI-assisted enterprise search (J1313) – Natural language search in the Search bar
  • AI-assisted easy filter – Streamline your filtering experience in Manage apps (aka SAP Fiori elements List Reports)
  • AI-assisted Smart Summarization  – Quick summaries generated from most Object/Detail pages (also known as Factsheets)
  • AI-assisted Error Explanation – Generates natural language descriptions and resolutions for error messages from most Fiori apps

 

  What this quick guide covers:

  • Business benefits
  • Impact on business users
  • Prerequisites
  • Activation steps
  • Monitoring and Support

Worth knowing:

  • As an administrator, you control when and where these features are enabled, and which users are authorized to use them.
  • As a business user, you control which features you use.

Nothing is forced. This lets you and your users adopt AI at your own pace. Users decide where they want assistance. They can continue to use the standard features alongside the AI-assisted features.

You can find more announcements of the latest UX improvements in SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS02 in SAP Blog SAP UX Update for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 FPS02 by Dr Tom Reiss.

Business Benefits

Why use these free features? Here you find the most important highlights – use the hyperlinks to view the full benefits on SAP Discovery Center.

AI-assisted enterprise search

  • Find stuff faster.
  • Estimated 50% time savings when searching business objects through natural language in the search field of the SAP Fiori Launchpad.

AI-assisted easy filter

  • Makes filtering through tables and lists easier & less tedious
  • Estimated 83% time savings when filtering in Manage apps (aka SAP Fiori elements list reports).

Worth knowing: Manage apps are the most widely available apps across all functional areas; most can be easily extended with Adapt UI (e.g. create a display-only variant); and an easy starting point for moving traditional GUI transaction users to modern browser-based apps.

AI-assisted smart summarization

  • Makes summarizing the status of a business object easier
  • Estimated 88% time saving when summarizing business object details (in SAP Fiori elements-based object pages, also sometimes known as factsheets).

Worth knowing: From most Manage apps (list reports) you can expand any row to see the business object details (object pages).

AI-assisted error explanation

  • Reduce training, minimize confusion and resolve issues faster.
  • Estimated 5% reduction in time to resolve errors.

Supported AI-Assisted SAP Fiori Apps

To give you some idea of which apps are supported, SAP Note 3692870 has an Attachment listing the SAP Fiori apps that support Easy Filter, Smart Summarization, and Easy Fill.  Although the note refers to the Public Edition, it also applies to SAP Fiori apps available in the Private Edition. 

  • SAP Note: 3692870 - Configuration of Base AI-Assisted Features in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. 

You will find even more apps in Private Cloud that support these features.  Look for UI Technology =  SAP Fiori elements in the app details found in the SAP Fiori apps reference library 2.0. 

 

Business Impact

What changes for users? As a business user, you control when and where you use the AI.

  • To use the AI-assisted search, you enable the search in your User Settings.  That setting also shows you which of your assigned searches supports natural language search (see hint below)
  • For all the other AI-assisted features, you just press the AI-assisted button or link to use the feature.

Hint: You can find the list of currently supported searches in SAP Note 3784221 - AI-assisted Enterprise Search SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition.  SAP is working on expanding the list of available searches. Yes, you can enable natural language search in your own custom searches – Refer your developers to annotation @EnterpriseSearch.nls - you might also suggest they use Joule for Consultants or Joule for Developers to provide some code examples.

 

AI-assisted enterprise search

Open the search bar. Select your search object. Type in what you are looking for and find the answer quickly.

For example: 

 

AI-assisted easy filter

Use this when you want to quickly filter the list without having to set each field individually.

Press the AI Filter button. Move your cursor to the natural language filter field. Type in what you are looking for. For example:

Worth knowing: Once filtered you save your filters as an app view for reuse.

 

AI-assisted smart summarization

For example, use this when a customer, supplier, or colleague asks: “what’s happening with this order/invoice/account/customer/supplier/budget?” 

When looking at object details, press button AI Summarize.

Select which parts of the object you want to include in the summary, and the AI generates a quick response. You can adjust the format if needed, then copy & paste into your preferred communication channel (email, MS Teams chat, etc.)

For example:

AI-assisted error explanation

When you get an error message, select the AI Generate Explanation link to get a natural language explanation and suggested next steps.

For example:

 

Prerequisites

Commercial/Legal

You will need to meet the requirements for using Base AI features in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition ( Legal $0 SKU ). At time of writing this means: you need to have signed the agreement for SAP AI Terms and the SAP AI Code of Conduct. You can find both agreements in your SAP Trust Center in the section Cloud Services.

There’s no cost and no AI Unit usage for these features, however agreements are still legally binding so do your usual due diligence.

Technical

These embedded AI-assisted features are powered by genAI models managed via ISLM.

ISLM = Intelligent Lifecycle Scenario Management. Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management (ISLM) is an ABAP-native framework that enables the integration and lifecycle management of AI scenarios within SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition. It provides connectivity to AI services and generative AI models available through Generative AI Hub in SAP AI Core on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), enabling customers to securely integrate AI capabilities into their business processes. You connect ISLM in your SAP S/4HANA solution to your SAP BTP AI Core using a Service Key.

To reduce effort for your administrator, SAP can configure the ISLM genAI model connection for you. The process is explained below in section Activation Steps. Even if you choose to have SAP set up the connection for you, your administrator will still need access to review & monitor the connection.

In SAP BTP (Business Technology Platform)  - for your Administrator

  • AI Core service enabled – this connects your system to the genAI model that powers the feature

 

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition – for your Administrator:

  • To review or configure the ISLM connection: SAP GUI Transactions ISLM_REUSE_CFGV, ISLM_CONN_MAP, OA2C_CONFIG, STRUST, SM59, SFW2.
  • For ISLM monitoring and troubleshooting: SAP GUI transaction codes ISLM_SLG1 or SLG1.
  • SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA launchpad must be active and assigned to your administrator and business users
  • SAP Fiori apps F4469 Intelligent Scenarios and F4470 Intelligent Scenario Management must be activated and assigned. These are part of the SAP Business Role Analytics Specialist (SAP_BR_ANALYTICS_SPECIALIST).

 

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition – for your Users:

  • For enterprise search – they must be assigned one or more of the supported natural language search objects in the search bar.  

 

Activation Steps

  1. Set up the ISLM Connection
  2. Activate the ISLM Scenario
  3. Prepare for testing
  4. Schedule the ISLM Turnkey

 

In a SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud Edition release, the steps you need to complete for the AI-Assisted features depend on ISLM.  The following ISLM Scenario IDs are provided:

  • For enterprise search: ESH_NLS_SEARCH
  • For easy filter: AIU_FILTER
  • For smart summarization: AIU_SUMMARIZATION
  • For error explanation: AIU_EXPLANATION

 

1. Set up the ISLM Connection

Worth knowing: These AI-assisted features use a Reuse Connection. With a reuse connection, the ISLM connection is shared across multiple AI-assisted features, so the configuration only needs to be performed once.

SAP can complete the ISLM Connection configuration step for you.  This is known as automated opt-in configuration.   

If you choose the manual (opt-out) configuration, SAP will issue the service key to you, and you will need to complete the ISLM Connection configuration manually.

You start the process in SAP for Me. Choosing opt-in or opt-out is explained in: Requesting Access to SAP AI Services on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) | SAP Help Portal

If you choose automated opt-in configuration you can skip to step 3 Activate the ISLM Scenario.

If you choose manual opt-out configuration:

  • You will need the service key and the OAuth Profile id from the Intelligent Scenario ID. You can find this in app F4469 Intelligent Scenarios.  Expand the ISLM Scenario Id to confirm the OAuth Profile id for the scenario. 
  • You create an OAuth Configuration in transaction OA2C_CONFIG.
  • You may also need to adjust trust certificate settings in STRUST and OA2C_CONFIG.
  • You create a connection of type G (HTTP Connection to External Server) in transaction SM59. You reference the OAuth Profile and OAuth Configuration.

To set up a reuse connection shared by multiple ISLM Scenario Ids you need to:

  1. Create a new entry in transaction ISLM_REUSE_CFGV (Intelligent Scenario Usage Type Connections) for the Usage Type  = Stateless – Without Embeddings.
  2. Enter Resource group = <blank>

Refer to the detailed advice in SAP Help: SAP S/4HANA - Intelligent Scenarios in ISLM - SAP Delivered Generative AI Scenarios section Maintain Intelligent Scenario Usage Type Connections

 

2. Activate the ISLM Scenario

Open app F4470 Intelligent Scenario Management. You find this in the Analytics space. 

Find the ISLM Scenario ID and expand the row.

You can search for the easy filter, smart summarization, and error explanation scenarios using keyword AIU.

You can search for the enterprise  model using keyword ESH.

Select > at the end of the row to expand the scenario id row. You will see a summary of the current model and its turnkey status.

In tab Models, if the model is not yet active, select the Model you want to activate.

Worth knowing: If this is the first time the model has been used the training will start automatically.

In tab Trainings, you can view the existing Trainings.  You can select the most recent training with status = Completed, and press Deploy to deploy it.

In tab Deployments, you can view the existing Deployments.  Select the most recent deployment with status = Deployed, and select option Activate for all. This makes the model available for use by all users.

Your model should now show that:

  • The model is Active
  • The training is Deployed
  • The deployment is Active for All

Refer to SAP Help: SAP S/4HANA - SAP Fiori launchpad - Administration Guide - Enabling AI-Assisted Features and SAP S/4HANA > Enterprise Search > AI-assisted Enterprise Search

 

3. Prepare for Testing

Before you can test you need to:

  1. Assign authorizations to your test users 
  2. Check the API (OData Service) has been activated
  3. Run quick checks to confirm the features are visible to users

a. Assign authorizations to test users

To make assigning authorizations easier, SAP provides predefined business catalogs. 

  • SAP_CORE_BC_AIU_FIL for easy filter
  • SAP_CORE_BC_AIU_SUM for smart summarization
  • SAP_CORE_BC_AIU_EXP for error explanation

Each of these catalogs contains a single reuse app. Adding the reuse app to the user's business role authorizes the user to access the matching AI feature across all supported SAP Fiori apps already assigned to them.

 

You can assign these business catalogs directly to your custom business roles.

Worth knowing: AI-assisted enterprise search does not need any additional authorizations. Your existing authorizations for CDS View-based search connectors apply.

 

b. Check the API (OData Service) is active

From the Launchpad Content Manager - Client-Specific (transaction /UI2/FLPCM_CUST), select the AI-assisted business catalog, and choose menu option Services > Check Services to confirm if the service is active.  If the service is not active, you need to activate it.

To minimize configuration effort and ensure consistent governance across your landscape, the recommended approach is to activate the API with the rapid activation task lists to:

  • Publish services needed for the AI-assisted features. For example OData Service Group AIU_UI_PROMPT
  • Capture the changes to transports
  • Audit trail the activation (monitor task list runs in transaction STC02).

For example, from the Launchpad Content Manager - Client-Specific , select the AI-assisted business catalog, select the menu option Services > Activate Services (STC02).  This will navigate to transaction STC02 passing the catalog to  SAP_FIORI_FCM_CATALOG_ACTIVATION. All you have to do is add your transport package in task "Set transport options for to be activate OData Services" and start the task list.  The task will activate the OData Service Group, set up the transport, and audit trail the activation for later review. 

Refer to SAP Blog SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA – Activating Apps by Business Catalog. For details on which settings to use in the task list in subsequent systems of your landscape, refer to SAP Whitepaper SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA - Rapid Activation Transport Move to Production Strategy

 

Example: In transaction /IWFND/V4_ADMIN you can review the activated service group AIU_UI_PROMPT. This service group contains the APIs used by easy filter, smart summarization, and error explanation.

c. Quick checks before Testing

You can do some quicks checks in your SAP Fiori launchpad to make sure the AI-assisted features are visible, before you notify test users.

For enterprise search, in the User Actions - Settings dialog, section Search, check the option for AI Natural Language Search appears.  Once selected, the list of supported natural language searches assigned to the user will be shown.

For easy filter, go to any supported Manage app, for example F3893 Manage Sales Orders - Version 2, and check the AI Filter button appears.

For smart summarization, go to any supported Manage app, for example F3893 Manage Sales Orders -  Version 2, expand a row to see the object page details, and check the AI Summarize button appears.

For error explanation, deliberately generate an error. For example, in app F3893 Manage Sales Orders - Version 2, create a new Sales Order and leave the Sold-To party empty. When the messages dialog appears, check the Generate Explanation button appears.

Refer to SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA - SAP Fiori launchpad - User Guide - Using AI-Assisted Features

 

4. Schedule the ISLM Turnkey

Once you have tested your AI-assisted features are working, your genAI model need to be regularly checked, retrained, redeployed, and reactivated.

Worth knowing: Retraining makes sure your model is optimized for current use, as your data and metadata changes over time in your system.

You use a Turnkey Schedule to automate this process.

IMPORTANT: Make sure you schedule the Turnkey – not a Planned Task.

  • Planned Task automates retraining only.
  • The Turnkey schedules retraining, redeployment, and reactivation.

In app F4470 Intelligent Scenario Management, find the scenario id and in column Turnkey you toggle Turnkey from OFF to ON.

 

Confirm the Recurrence Pattern schedule, i.e. how often you want the retraining to run. Use the Edit button if you want to change it.

Press Create Turnkey Schedule.

The turnkey should now be scheduled. The Turnkey toggle will show Turnkey = ON.

Hint: If there any issues with setting up the scheduling, you will find log details in transaction ISLM_SLG1.

 

Expand the ISLM scenario id row. In the tab Turnkey, you can use the subtabs to review the Turnkey Schedules and the history of Turnkey Runs.

Hint: If there any issues with setting up the Turnkey Scheduling, you will find log details in transaction ISLM_SLG1.

 

In the Turnkey Runs tab, you can see when the turnkey was last run and if it was successful. You can check messages using the Message icon.

Hint: If there any issues with the Turnkey Runs, you will find the log details in transaction ISLM_SLG1.

 

 

Refer to SAP Help: SAP S/4HANA - ISLM - Advanced Configuration and Features - Turnkey - Create a Turnkey Schedule

 

Support and Monitoring

As an administrator, you can use transaction ISLM_SLG1 to review detailed logs.

When running this transaction, the subtypes help you focus.

 

ISLM Main Sub Types in ISLM_SLG1

Purpose

MODEL

Model changes and extensions

INFERENCE / MINFERENCE

Model consumption at runtime

MDEPLOYMENT

Model deployment

PREREQ_RUN

Prerequisite Checks 

METADATA_SYNC / STATUS_SYNC

Metadata / Status synchronization with genAI model provider

ACTIVITY_REQUEST

Model is called at runtime

TURNKEY / TURNKEY_APPLICATION

Turnkey activities via Turnkey Schedule

PLANNED_TSK_CD / PLANNED_TSK_EXE

Training activities via Planned Tasks

 

Worth knowing: ISLM requires the following jobs to be scheduled. You can view these in transaction SJOBREPO and monitor job runs in transaction SM37.

 

ISLM Jobs in SJOBREPO

Purpose

SAP_ISLM_SCHEDULER

Runs in Client 000 – out of scope in other clients

Checks if training is needed based on the Turnkey schedule. If there is a scheduled job, it triggers SAP_ISLM_PROCESSOR to train the model

SAP_ISLM_PROCESSOR

Triggers training of the model

SAP_ISLM_SYNC_SCHEDULER

Runs Metadata sync (scenario versions, pipelines, parameters, etc.) and Status synchronization with the remote genAI model provider

SAP_ISLM_PREREQ_CHK_PROCESSOR

Runs the Prerequisite checks

SAP_ISLM_INFERENCE_DOWNLOAD / SAP_ISLM_INFERENCE_ RES_CLEANUP

Downloads inference results / cleans up downloads

 

Becoming a SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA Guru

You’ll find much more on our community topic page for SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA.

entry.title: Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management (ISLM): Availability Matrix Across SAP Products
entry.content:
“Is ISLM available on my system? Which AI capabilities can I use today?” These are among the most common questions we hear from customers and partners exploring ISLM and its capabilities.

This blog provides an overview of Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management (ISLM) availability across ABAP-based SAP products.

Bringing AI into enterprise business processes

Enterprises are moving fast with AI. But embedding artificial intelligence into business processes comes with real challenges: complex integration, fragmented lifecycles, scaling beyond proof-of-concepts, and governance and compliance requirements.

Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management (ISLM) is built to address these challenges. As an ABAP-native framework, ISLM helps integrate and operate AI within SAP business applications, with unified lifecycle management and enterprise-grade governance. ISLM Supports both SAP-delivered and custom AI use cases.

From Classical Machine Learning and Tabular AI to Generative AI, ISLM brings AI scenarios under one framework. Together with the ABAP AI SDK, powered by ISLM, it enables low-code integration of generative AI into ABAP applications, including access to large language models through the Generative AI Hub in SAP AI Core. The result is lower development effort, more consistent operations, and AI closer to business processes. 

ISLM Availability: Products, Releases, and Capabilities

ISLM is available across SAP S/4HANA On-Premise, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, and SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment. ISLM supports delivery of SAP-provided AI scenarios in SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP).

ISLM provides an evolving set of AI capabilities across SAP products, with new capabilities introduced progressively with each release. Initial SAP HANA ML functionality, LLM-based scenarios, Generative AI with Orchestration, and SAP RPT follow different release timelines. In particular, broader Orchestration and SAP RPT enablement for SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment is planned for 2708, as shown in the matrix below. entry.title: Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private - What's New in 2025 FPS02
entry.content:
Every upgrade cycle, the gap between available and activated widens, not because teams don't care, but because connecting the dots between what shipped, what it changes, and what you need to do is harder than it should be. SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 FPS02 ships 996 innovations across 15+ lines of business, including 15 AI-embedded capabilities and 622 net-new features, all available now. This post gives you the short version of what matters, where to find the full picture, and how the Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private closes the activation gap for your team.

         

 

  • What's New in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition
  • SAP Best Practices for 2025 FPS02
  • Product Enablement
  • Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private
  • Future Planning: 2025 FPS03
  • Connect with Us

 

What's New in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition

2025 FPS02 ships 996 innovations applicable to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, of which 622 are net-new capabilities alongside 345 enhancements to existing functions and 28 deprecations. That breadth spans every major line of business: Finance (150 items), Cross Applications (174), Supply Chain (101), Manufacturing (87), Asset Management (59), R&D/Engineering (53), and more.

Not all 996 demand the same attention. Here are five high-impact areas worth reviewing first:

1. AI-Assisted Filtering, Error Explanation, and Summarization — embedded in SAP Fiori Elements (App Platform / UX)

Three new AI capabilities are now embedded directly into SAP Fiori elements-based applications in Private Edition — exclusively for PE in this release:

  • AI-Assisted Easy Filter: users describe filter criteria in natural language instead of configuring them manually. Particularly relevant for Finance, Procurement, and Planning users working with complex filter sets daily.
  • AI-Assisted Error Explanation:
  • when users encounter an error on an object page, the system explains the issue and recommends resolution steps in plain language. Reduces support escalations and speeds up transaction completion.
  • AI-Assisted Smart Summarization: object pages can generate a contextual summary of the record's contents, useful for approvals, audits, and management reviews.

All three are new capabilities in FPS02 and require activation. You can explore all 15 AI-category items for Private Edition directly in the What's New Viewer via this filtered URL: AI/Joule innovations in FPS02 → What's New Viewer.

2. Joule API for Web Dynpro Applications (App Platform / ABAP)

Web Dynpro apps embedded in the SAP Fiori launchpad can now integrate with Joule via the new IF_WD_JOULE_API interface. This extends Joule's conversational capabilities into legacy Web Dynpro transactions, a significant unlock for customers with custom or older apps still running on Web Dynpro. Available for both SAP S/4HANA and Private Edition.

3. AI-Assisted Enterprise Search in Manufacturing

AI-assisted natural language search is now available in Production Planning and Control ("AI-Assisted Enterprise Search for Production Planning and Control") and more broadly across manufacturing business data ("AI Assisted Search for Business Data"). Users can query production orders, materials, and resources in plain language without manual search configuration.

4. Expanded Joule Capabilities Across the Suite (Cross Applications)

The "Joule Capabilities Supported" update in Cross Applications reflects a broader expansion of Joule's transactional coverage. Combined with the new Joule Web Client API for Web Dynpro, this release meaningfully extends the surface area of AI-assisted work available in Private Edition.

5. Configuring User Default Parameters for the SAP Fiori Launchpad (App Platform)

Administrators can now configure default parameter values for standard and custom SAP Fiori applications via the Launchpad App Manager. Users benefit from pre-populated filter fields without manual setup each session, a targeted improvement for high-frequency transactional roles. Scope: SAP S/4HANA and Private Edition. New capability in FPS02.

Customer Action Required vs. auto-on: Of the 996 innovations, 342 are linked to scope items, these are the items most likely to require customer review, activation, or configuration before users benefit. The remaining ~654 are platform-level changes or automatically available post-upgrade. Use the What's New Viewer with the Scope Item filter to generate your team's action list quickly.

 

SAP Best Practices for 2025 FPS02

New system capabilities only deliver value when underlying business process designs reflect them. With 2025 FPS02, the SAP Best Practices for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition content library now contains 433 processes in SAP Signavio Process Navigator under the S4O solution scenario, updated to reflect the new and changed functionality in this release.

The scope items most affected align with the top innovation areas in FPS02:

  • Finance: Record-to-Report (fixed assets, financial close), Treasury, and Controlling scope items updated to reflect AI-assisted features and API expansions.
  • Asset Management / Maintenance Management: the most extensively updated area in FPS02, with new scope items for Maintenance Order Relationships, Task Planning Design, Industrial System management, and multiple new OData APIs.
  • Service: Call type 6 (Service Order with Advanced Execution) now supported in Manage Maintenance Plans and Manage Maintenance Items apps, moving these processes into the Fiori-native flow.

Three process areas to review now:

  1. Maintenance Order Relationships: graphical operation sequencing (Asset Management; scope items 4HH, 4HI, BH1, BJ2)
    • The new Manage Maintenance Order Relationships app (F8506) enables graphical visualization and management of operation dependencies within and across maintenance orders. For customers whose maintenance planning spans multiple work centers or requires sequencing logic, this is a process redesign opportunity — not just a new app. Review updated scope items for Reactive, Proactive, and Improvement Maintenance.
  2. Service Order with Advanced Execution: Maintenance Plans now in Fiori (Service; scope item 7GA) 
    • Previously available only in WebDynpro, call type 6 maintenance plans and items are now manageable in the Fiori-based Manage Maintenance Plans (F5325) and Manage Maintenance Items (F5356) apps. If your team hasn't migrated this process to Fiori, FPS02 removes the final blocker. Review the 7GA scope item for updated process flows and test scripts.
  3. Manufacturing AI Search — Production Planning and Control process update (Manufacturing) 
    • AI-assisted enterprise search is now embedded in the standard Production Planning process. The scope items for Demand Planning, MRP, and Production Order Management should be reviewed for updated process descriptions that reflect natural language search as a standard workflow step.

How to find FPS02 delta content in Process Navigator

  • Navigate to SAP Signavio Process Navigator via SAP for Me → select the S4O solution scenario for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition → filter by release 2025 FPS02. The delta content — updated scope items, new test scripts, revised process flows — is versioned by release and available without a customer system login.

 

Product Enablement

The enablement for 2025 FPS02 is available now via the Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private, accessible through SAP Enterprise Support on support.sap.com.

What's available today:

  • What's New documentation (version 2025.002) The full What's New content for FPS02 is live on the SAP Help Portal. Each of the 996 items links directly to its help topic, so you can go from innovation description to implementation guidance in one click. The Upgrade Guide for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 (version 3.0, dated October 7, 2026) is published alongside it and covers upgrade prerequisites, simplification items, and deprecated functionality.
  • SAP Signavio Process Navigator — S4O solution scenario As described in Section 2, the S4O scenario in Process Navigator is updated with FPS02 delta content. Process flows, test scripts, and accelerators for scope items with FPS02 changes are live and accessible to S-users via SAP for Me.
  • Release Navigator on Release Ready (support.sap.com) The Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private is available today. It centralizes key dates, feature highlights, scope item links, enablement blogs, and support materials for each release, organized specifically for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition. This is the starting point for anyone who wants to go deeper than this blog post.
  • SAP Learning content No SAP Learning courses have been published specifically for 2025 FPS02 at the time of writing. Existing SAP Learning content for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 covers foundational capabilities and remains relevant as an onboarding foundation for this release. As FPS02 capabilities mature in customer systems, course updates are expected, bookmark https://learning.sap.com and filter to "SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025" to catch new content when it arrives.

Who needs system access vs. what's publicly available

  • The What's New Viewer, Upgrade Guide, and Release Navigator content on support.sap.com require an S-user login but not a customer production system. SAP Signavio Process Navigator requires an S-user via SAP for Me. Partners and consultants can access all of this before their customer's system is available, which means there is no reason to wait until upgrade completion to start preparing.

 

Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private

The Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private is a curated, role-appropriate digital guide delivered by SAP Enterprise Support. It is built specifically for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition customers, partners, and consultants, and it solves a concrete problem: the relevant release content is scattered across SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, SAP Learning, and SAP Signavio, and most teams find what they need too late or not at all.

Release Navigator pulls this together in one place: key dates, feature highlights organized by line of business, scope item links, release notes, learning assets, and SAP Community blog posts, all filtered to Private Edition and the current release.

  • This tool is built for Private Edition: The Public Cloud release cadence and tooling are different. Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private is scoped and curated specifically for the Private Edition deployment model and the quarterly FPS release rhythm.
  • How to access: Here is a link to the Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private (S-user required). Partners and consultants with an S-user login — even without a customer system contract — can access the tool and all its FPS02 content directly.

 

Future Planning: 2025 FPS03

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition follows a two-year major release cycle with three Feature Package Stacks (FPS) in between, each FPS delivered approximately every six months. The 2025 base release (FPS00) shipped in October 2025; FPS01 followed in approximately April 2026; FPS02 is generally available as of October 2026.

What's next:

  • 2025 FPS03 — scheduled for the week of March 1–5, 2027. FPS03 will be the final FPS in the 2025 release line before SAP's next major base release.
  • SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 carries mainstream maintenance through December 2032 — giving customers seven years from the base release date to plan their next major upgrade.

Why this matters now: If your team is still on an earlier release, FPS02 is the current generally available target. Customers running 2023 FPS02 or earlier should check their maintenance window against SAP's Product Availability Matrix, end-of-mainstream-maintenance dates for older FPS versions are triggered by the availability of newer releases.

For forward planning: The SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition innovations roadmap give visibility into planned capabilities before they ship. Teams who review the roadmap before each FPS cycle can pre-configure processes, brief stakeholders, and build test plans in advance, rather than discovering new capabilities after upgrade.

 

Connect with Us

Your feedback is essential to shaping future improvements to the release navigator. We invite you to:
