entry.title: Exploring AI and key innovations in SAP Cloud ERP Private 2025 FPS2
entry.content:
SAP is building the Autonomous Enterprise — an operating model where AI is not a separate tool but a force embedded directly into the operational core, executing work end to end. The SAP Cloud ERP Private 2025 FPS2 (also referred to as SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 FPS2) release accelerates this shift, expanding agentic AI across finance, supply chain, asset management, sales, service, and product design.

At the top sits Joule — the new engagement layer where people, data, workflows, and agents come together across SAP systems and beyond. Underneath, the SAP Autonomous Suite reimagines how enterprises run through three coordinated layers:

  • Joule Assistants are role-aligned AI teammates — each designed around a specific business function such as financial closing, cash management, or logistics. They understand your context and coordinate the right agents to deliver the outcome you need.
  • Joule Agents are the specialized doers. Each agent handles a specific multi-step task — calculating accruals, screening maintenance requests, resolving invoice discrepancies — reasoning over live business data and acting autonomously within defined guardrails.
  • Embedded AI features power everyday Fiori applications with natural-language search, smart summarization, AI-assisted filtering, and error explanation — intelligence built directly into the screen, no agent orchestration required.

Industry AI adds vertical depth — process knowledge, compliance rules, and data models specific to your industry, embedded from day one. And the SAP Business AI Platform provides the foundation everything runs on: unified data, business context, and enterprise-grade governance.

 

*Disclaimer: The Joule Assistants and Agents described in this post are currently available through SAP's Early Adopter Care (EAC) program. General availability is planned to begin in Q4 2026, with rollout continuing into Q1 2027. Not all agents require SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 FPS2 — minimum system requirements vary by agent, and support for additional releases is being continuously extended through downports. For the latest on which releases support which agents, refer to SAP Note 3789370, which is updated on an ongoing basis, and the SAP Discovery Center. All other AI innovations covered in this post (embedded AI features, Joule skills, and machine learning scenarios) are generally available with the 2025 FPS2 release unless noted otherwise. This blog is a living document and will be updated as new assistants and agents become available in the coming weeks and months. The information here reflects publicly available SAP product documentation and roadmap materials as of October 2026. All forward-looking statements are subject to change.

 

With this release, SAP significantly expands both the number of assistants and the depth of agent coverage across the suite. Here is what is new.

Part A: Joule Assistants and Agents

 

Finance: Autonomous Intelligence Across the Financial Lifecycle

Finance is the largest area of AI investment in FPS2, with new agents and assistants organized across the Autonomous Finance portfolio — from accounting and close, to treasury, revenue management, and compliance.

Financial Closing Assistant

 

The Financial Closing Assistant orchestrates the agents managing the period close, with users controlling each agent's level of engagement for handling journal postings, clearing activities, and analysis. Its tasks include: clearing receivables and payables; calculating and posting accounting accruals; posting journal entries; resolving errors and detecting anomalies in asset accounting; analyzing financial consistency and surfacing bottlenecks; reconciling goods receipt/invoice receipt and intercompany transactions (including matching unstructured intercompany invoices); managing fixed-asset master data and reviewing general ledger accounts; and clearing general ledger balances with final review, KPI analysis, and executive-summary generation. assistant is coordinated by the Financial Closing Orchestration Agent and includes the Journal Entry Agent for recommending and posting general-ledger entries with an evidence trail, the Accounting Accruals Agent for analyzing historical data and preparing accrual journal entries, the Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent, the Financial Consistency Analysis Agent for identifying hidden process inconsistencies and the Asset Accounting Anomaly Detection Agent for flagging potentially inaccurate postings. (SAP Discovery Center | Learn more).

 

 

Accounts Receivable Assistant

 

The Accounts Receivable Assistant helps finance teams accelerate cash collection, resolve disputes efficiently, and manage credit risk proactively, providing a 360-degree customer view that surfaces overdue items, balances, dispute cases, promises to pay, resubmissions, and contact history. Its capabilities span collection worklist management, dispute management, and dunning insights — focusing collectors on critical accounts, surfacing next-best-action recommendations, preparing customer communications, creating and resolving disputes from emails or Joule prompts, and analyzing payment history with AI-based matching and aging-pattern analysis. The assistant coordinates specialized agents: the Accounts Receivable Orchestration Agent, the Collection Account Preparation Agent for delivering instant account insights and preparing collection calls, the Dispute Creation Agent for creating dispute cases and validating documents and duplicates, the Dispute Resolution Agent for providing context and recommending resolution actions, the Dunning Insights Agent for analyzing payment history and providing AR recommendations and the Receivable Account Analysis Agent for visibility into balances, invoices, aging, disputes, and dunning levels.(SAP Discovery Center | ).

 

 

Accounts Payable Assistant

 

The Accounts Payable Assistant transforms AP with AI-powered automation — eliminating manual payments, automating bank validations, and resolving exceptions instantly while predicting payment risks, detecting clearing patterns, and surfacing real-time insights on DPO, aging, and cash flow. Its capabilities span six areas: payment inquiry, which captures requests, triggers payments, and sends status updates; pre-validation, which validates attributes, checks compliance, performs risk checks, and recommends fixes; bank validation, which verifies supplier bank accounts, automates risk checks, and recommends corrective actions; exceptions, which flags, explains, and routes payment exceptions; vendor analytics, which tracks DPO, cash flow, and discount opportunities and identifies operational improvements; and reconciliation, which reconciles statements and highlights discrepancies. The assistant coordinates with specialized agents: the Accounts Payable Orchestration Agent and the Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent for AI-based matching and aging-pattern analysis to generate clearing recommendations. (SAP Discovery Center | ).

 

Recurring Receivables Assistant

 

The Recurring Receivables Assistant helps finance teams automate and optimize the order-to-cash process for recurring billing and subscription-based business models, deploying finance agents that accelerate cash collection, resolve disputes, and identify and act on revenue at risk. Its capabilities span convergent invoicing, subscription contract changes, invoice correction orchestration, collections prioritization, dispute resolution, 360-degree customer account visibility, and payment matching with continuously improving matching rules. The assistant coordinates with specialized agents: the Subscription Lifecycle Agent for managing subscription contract changes with compliant updates, the Convergent Invoice Execution Agent for detecting invoice issues and executing compliant fixes and the Collection Insights Agent for recommending next-best actions prioritized by cash impact and customer insights.(SAP Discovery Center | ).

 

Sales: Agentic Order Fulfillment and Expanded Conversational Capabilities

Sales Operations Assistant

 

The Sales Operations Assistant enables sales teams to quickly identify fulfillment issues, receive recommended resolutions, and create or update sales documents directly in their workflow — minimizing manual rework and delays, reducing order-to-cash cycle time, and improving customer satisfaction. Its capabilities span two core areas: order entry, which supports uploading unstructured purchase-order files, extracting and validating data, reviewing order requests, and converting them into sales orders; and order monitoring and issue resolution, which covers supply, credit, billing, and delivery issues — including recommending corrective actions, removing blocks, and creating or updating sales documents after human approval. The assistant coordinates with specialized agents: the Billing Block Resolution Agent, the Credit Block Issues Resolution Agent, the Delivery Issue Resolution Agent, and the Supply Issue Resolution Agent (SAP Discovery Center | ).

 

 

Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Logistics

The supply chain and manufacturing areas receive targeted AI enhancements in FPS2, with a focus on production planning intelligence, quality management automation, and warehouse operations support.

Logistics Assistant

 

The Logistics Assistant brings AI-driven coordination to warehouse operations, helping keep day-to-day logistics running efficiently. In this release for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, it focuses on two critical areas: batch lifecycle management and warehouse resource optimization. On the batch side, the assistant continuously monitors batch expiration across inventory and triggers actions to minimize waste — ensuring perishable or time-sensitive goods are consumed or moved before they expire. On the warehouse floor, it facilitates optimal resource allocation by analyzing workload patterns and proactively flagging potential resource shortages before they impact operations. The assistant coordinates with two specialized agents: the Batch Optimization Agent, which autonomously tracks expiry timelines and initiates corrective actions, and the Warehouse Workload Optimization Agent, which balances labor and capacity to keep throughput on target (SAP Discovery Center | Learn more).

 

 

Asset Management: A New Level of Intelligence for Maintenance and Operations

Asset management receives the most comprehensive agent expansion in this release, with a suite of new Joule Agents — orchestrated by the Asset Operations Assistant — designed to support the entire maintenance lifecycle from equipment onboarding to job debriefing.

 

Asset Operations Assistant

 

The Asset Operations Assistant orchestrates AI agents across reliability, maintenance planning, scheduling, and execution to turn asset signals into coordinated maintenance action and improve uptime. It interprets equipment signals and requests to prioritize work, aligns resources and readiness, and uses execution outcomes to continuously improve asset performance. Its tasks include: assessing asset alerts and recommending next-best actions; creating and prioritizing maintenance work based on asset conditions, business priorities, and operational needs; optimizing maintenance schedules and workforce assignments; and briefing technicians and summarizing completed work. The assistant coordinates six specialized agents: the Equipment Insights Agent for complete equipment insights supporting better decisions, planning, and reliability; the Maintenance Event Planning Agent for avoiding disruptions with real-time insights, smart updates, and planning support; the Maintenance Job Debrief Agent for streamlining maintenance job debriefs with AI-driven recommendations and insights; the Maintenance Request Initiation Agent for instantly creating and routing maintenance requests from natural language inputs; the Maintenance Task List Management Agent for automating task list creation, boosting consistency, and reducing effort; and the Operational Maintenance Planning Agent for avoiding disruptions with real-time insights, smart updates, and planning support (SAP Discovery Center | Learn more).

 

R&D / Engineering

 

Product Design Assistant

 

The Product Design Assistant is an AI-driven system of agents that connects data across product development and downstream processes. It analyzes product information, supports change decisions, ensures compliance, and coordinates collaboration — helping teams move faster, reduce rework, and deliver higher-quality products. Its tasks include: analyzing product designs, recipes, and specifications; preparing product changes including scoping and assessing impacts; validating compliance and requirements across product and recipe data; extracting, classifying, and improving product data quality; setting up collaborations, tracking tasks, and creating notifications; and preparing product data for handover to production and supply chain execution. The assistant coordinates two specialized agents: the Change Record Management Agent for reducing cost and accelerating time-to-market and the Product Data Maintenance Agent for assisting design engineers who work with product master data in SAP S/4HANA (SAP Discovery Center | Learn more).

 

Procurement

 

Receiving Assistant

The Receiving Assistant is a new Joule Assistant for procurement that simplifies goods receipt, service entry sheet processing, and returns by automating tasks, streamlining workflows, and guiding users through complex receiving scenarios. In this release, the assistant introduces the Return Goods to Supplier Agent — a specialized agent that detects goods with slow or no movement in inventory and optimizes and automates the returns process back to the supplier. Instead of requiring procurement or warehouse teams to manually identify stagnant stock, investigate root causes, and initiate return purchase orders, the agent continuously monitors inventory movement patterns and triggers the returns workflow autonomously. This reduces the manual effort involved in identifying returnable goods, accelerates the returns cycle, and helps organizations recover value from unused or slow-moving inventory. The result: lower carrying costs, improved working capital, and a cleaner inventory position — all driven by machine learning rather than periodic manual reviews (SAP | Learn more).

 

Part B: Embedded AI Innovations

 

AI-assisted enterprise search in the SAP Fiori launchpad to search for form bundles and contract objects

 

AI-assisted enterprise search in the SAP Fiori launchpad extends natural-language search to form bundles and contract objects, allowing users to type plain-language queries in the launchpad search bar and retrieve relevant results without navigating complex filter structures. The feature targets a larger and more specific result set from less-specific queries, reducing the time users spend locating the right form bundle or contract object. It builds on the broader AI-assisted enterprise search capability already available in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for objects such as sales orders, billing documents, and purchase orders — and is listed as a future release for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition (SAP Discovery Center).

 

AI-Assisted Enterprise Search for Service Contracts

This feature extends natural language search in the SAP Fiori launchpad to service contracts, enabling users to find contracts using plain language queries with instant responses. It eliminates the need to learn system syntax or complex filters, simplifying adoption and reducing training needs while delivering results in a single search interaction.

 

AI-Assisted Defect Creation (Quality Management)

Joule now enables quality engineers and technicians to create defect records through natural language — including from uploaded source documents such as invoices, delivery notes, or photographs of a defective part. Instead of manually navigating screens and populating fields, users simply describe the issue or attach a document, and Joule extracts the key data — material number, batch, quantity, reference documents, customer or supplier information, defect description, and defect code — then calls the Defects API to create a pre-filled record. The capability supports Generic Defects, Production Defects, and Warehouse Defects (types 06, 07, and 08). Once created, users review and complete the defect in the Manage Defects app. Under the hood, the feature runs on the QM_DEFECT_DOCSUMMARY intelligent scenario and requires activation through Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management (ISLM). Available from 2025 FPS02 (SAP Help).

 

AI-Assisted Enterprise Search for Bill of Distribution (BOD) 

Enables natural language search for bill of distribution data, simplifying navigation and accelerating access to critical logistics information for planning and distribution teams.

 

AI-Assisted Enterprise Search for Batches in the SAP Fiori Launchpad

This feature extends natural language search to batches within the SAP Fiori launchpad, displaying key data including shelf-life expiration date, manufacturing date, batch status, country of origin, supplier, material, and plant. It enhances the search experience by allowing users to find batch data using everyday language.

 

AI-Generated Business Insights in Cost Center Review Booklet (Finance)

 AI-generated summaries now enhance the cost center review booklet, providing deeper financial oversight by analyzing and validating both actual and planned cost data. Business users get faster, more informed analysis with insights that would previously have required manual review of multiple reports.

 

 

Performance and Flexibility for Behavioral Insights (Collections Management for Contract Accounting)

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition includes an AI-supported capability called Behavioral Insights for Contract Accounting — a machine learning solution that analyzes historical customer data to predict and explain payment risk. Collection specialists use these risk scores and insights to quickly identify high-risk accounts, optimize collection strategies, and reduce outstanding debts and write-offs. Results integrate directly into existing dunning and collections workflows.

The 2025 FPS2 release strengthens this capability across three dimensions. First, performance enhancements now support significantly larger datasets within the models, enabling organizations with high-volume receivables to run predictions at scale. Second, flexibility enhancements introduce support for multiple contract account categories within a single solution — a change that directly enables public sector organizations managing multiple tax types to leverage behavioral insights across their full portfolio. Third, a new ability to accommodate test datasets where the data may not be current makes it easier and faster to validate and deploy machine learning scenarios in non-production environments.

A key architectural advantage remains: the solution keeps data in place within SAP S/4HANA, eliminating the need for data extraction or replication. This reduces deployment risk, accelerates time to value, and ensures that sensitive customer data never leaves the system boundary.

 

 

Create Sales Orders from Unstructured Data with Document AI (Sales)

Internal sales representatives can now create sales orders directly from purchase order files in PDF, email, or image formats. The system leverages premium Document AI (AnyDox) to automatically extract file information and propose values for sales order fields — with multi-language support and instant learning capabilities. This significantly reduces manual data entry and accelerates order processing, especially in high-volume environments.

 

AI-Assisted Management of Expiring Service Contracts with Joule Skill (Service)

This feature enables users to search for expiring service contract items within a user-defined time frame via Joule and run extension scenarios including configuring auto-renewal, renewing and creating new service contracts, renewing entire contracts or specific line items, and providing quick actions for expiring contracts. It allows service teams to manage contract tasks through natural language requests, providing fast navigation and targeted guidance for renewing or extending contracts.

 

Joule-Based Search and Status Update of Service Contracts with Joule Skill (Service)

Users can now search for service contracts or contract items by employee and product name directly in Joule, and change lifecycle status to "released" or "complete" within the same conversational experience. This combines search and updates in a single interaction, reducing clicks and context switching while minimizing administrative overhead for contract managers.

 

 

AI-Assisted Processing of Incoming Quality Certificates

This capability, cross-ported from SAP Cloud ERP, automates the extraction and validation of data from supplier quality certificates. It delivers immediate efficiency gains by reducing manual effort in quality management — a high-usage area where even small improvements have a significant impact. In parallel, Joule for App Navigation in Quality Management now enables users to instantly navigate to more than 15 core QM Fiori apps using natural language queries.

 

Master Data Management

 

Joule for Data Provider Integration in Business Partner Governance

This feature enables users to search for business partner reference records from external data providers directly within Joule, display details including name, address, and identification numbers, and create a business partner from a selected reference record with pre-populated fields. It simplifies data governance through a conversational interface, improves data quality, and reduces manual entry by transferring reference data directly into the creation flow.

 

Joule for Business Partners — Central Governance

Users can now ask Joule in natural language to search, display, and edit business partner data, including address, communication, bank, and identification data. This delivers a consumer-grade experience for master data processing, increasing effectiveness, speed, and automation in business partner governance. Available in cloud-ready mode in SAP Master Data Governance.

 

 

AI-Assisted Validation Rule Creation in Joule

Joule can now create validation rules using AI, automatically deriving values such as the base table from a provided description. It also checks for duplicates to determine if a similar rule already exists in the system — increasing efficiency, reducing manual effort, and maintaining system integrity.

 

User-Experience

 

AI-Assisted Filtering Using Natural Language for SAP Fiori Elements Apps

Users can now filter list report applications built with SAP Fiori elements using conversational terms alongside system-defined filters. The feature supports query reuse, including saving favorite queries and accessing last-used ones — making data access more intuitive across all Fiori elements-based applications.

 

AI-Assisted Explanation of Errors in SAP Fiori Elements-Based Applications

This feature provides AI-generated explanations for error messages in SAP Fiori elements apps, offering solution proposals directly within the framework. It increases productivity by minimizing downtime from data entry errors and reduces training time through clear, natural-language guidance.

 

AI-Assisted Smart Summarization of Application Content

Users can generate AI-driven summaries for business object pages in SAP Fiori elements applications, then edit and copy them for sharing with stakeholders or external parties. It simplifies access to vital business data through one-click functionality and boosts productivity by supporting faster, informed decision-making.

 

Note: This blog focuses on the AI and Joule innovations that bring the most meaningful business impact in this release. It is not an exhaustive list of all enhancements — for the full scope of what's new, check out the resources linked at the end. A comprehensive release blog covering all innovations across every Line of Business is being prepared by Harish Mangtani and will be published in the coming days. Follow Harish on SAP Community to get notified when it goes live.

 

Looking Ahead

With the 2025 FPS2 release, SAP Cloud ERP Private (also referred to as SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition) continues to demonstrate that the future of enterprise work is not about adding AI on top — it is about building intelligence directly into the fabric of business processes. Every agent and assistant introduced in this release is designed to reduce manual effort, improve data quality, support faster decisions, and ultimately help your teams focus on the work that matters most.

The innovations in this release are part of SAP's broader vision for the Autonomous Enterprise — where Joule Assistants coordinate specialized Agents across all business functions, powered by SAP's deep process expertise and real-time business data. The pipeline of assistants and agents continues to expand rapidly. Additional assistants are expected to follow in the near term. This blog will be updated as new capabilities reach Early Adopter Care or general availability. For the latest status on all available agents, check the SAP Discovery Center and SAP Note 3789370.

If you want to explore the full scope of innovations in this release — including non-AI enhancements — I encourage you to check out the following resources:

  • What's New in SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 
  • AI Roadmap for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition
  • SAP Discovery Center- AI Catalog
  • SAP Notes 3523238 - Navigational and Transactional capabilities with Joule
  • What's New for Joule - Joule Capabilities Guide
  • Exploring the Autonomous Finance Portfolio (SAP Learning)
  • Discover joule assistants by business function and capability

If you'd like to stay informed about upcoming features, deep dives, and enablement content, make sure to follow updates tagged with PSCC_Enablement in the SAP Community. You're also welcome to connect with me on LinkedIn: linkedin@yannickpeterschmitt and in the SAP Community: Community@Yannick_PTT for more insights and continuous updates.

entry.title: S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition (006) - OS再起動
entry.content:
SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Editionをご利用いただく中で、例えば以下のようなケースにおいて、OS再起動を実施したい場面があるかと存じます。

  • パフォーマンス問題への対応として、アプリケーションおよびDBの再起動だけでなく、OSも再起動したい場合
  • 定期的にOS再起動を実施したい場合
  • OSカーネルパラメータの変更を恒久的に反映させたい場合

今回は、SR(サービスリクエスト)を利用して、OS再起動をRISE側へ依頼する方法についてご説明いたします。
OS再起動の依頼には、以下のSRテンプレートをご利用ください。

ご利用いただくSRテンプレート: Restart System with Reboot option

 

シナリオ1 - APサーバのOS再起動

 

SRにて依頼する際は、AP（アプリケーション）のSID（システムID）を選択のうえ、Service Parameterに以下をご指定ください。

  • Restart Scope: System
  • Set system message (for ABAP systems): ABAPシステムにおいて、メンテナンス期間中に表示するシステムメッセージを設定するかどうかを指定する項目です。
  • OS reboot Required: true
  • Reason for Restart: リストからOS再起動の理由を選択してください。

 

シナリオ2 - APおよびDBサーバのOS再起動

 

SRにて依頼する際は、DB（データベース）のSID（システムID）を選択のうえ、Service Parameterに以下をご指定ください。
Service Parameterの指定内容は、シナリオ1と同様です。ポイントとして、DBのSIDを選択された場合は、DBサーバだけでなくAPサーバのOS再起動も併せて実施されます。

 

まとめ

 

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private EditionにおいてSRを利用し、OS再起動をRISE側へ依頼する方法についてご紹介いたしました。
SRテンプレート「Restart System with Reboot option」では、APおよびDBサービスの再起動を実施することも可能ですが、こちらについては別の機会にご紹介させていただきます。

entry.title: Release Highlights 2025 FPS02 : advanced ATP in SAP Cloud ERP, Private Edition
entry.content:
As SAP’s flagship solution, advanced ATP (aATP) in SAP ERP Private Cloud delivers intelligent, real-time order confirmations based on supply and capacity constraints, helping organizations strengthens supply chain performance while ensuring accurate delivery commitments.  By connecting SAP Integrated Business Planning with SAP Cloud ERP, Order Promising enables seamless alignment between supply chain planning and execution across the order-to-cash process.

 
The October 2026 (2025 FPS02) release of SAP Advanced Available-to-Promise (aATP) for SAP Cloud ERP, Private Edition introduces a comprehensive set of enhancements designed to strengthen order fulfillment capabilities. Key innovations span backorder processing, product substitution, stock visibility, and API extensibility, enabling greater flexibility, transparency, and efficiency in order promising and fulfillment processes.
 
Here's a summary of the key highlights and what they mean for our customers.
 

 

Alternative-Based Confirmation (ABC) using new product interchangeability master data

 


With Alternative-Based Confirmation customers can improve fulfilment reliability and maximize product availability by automatically identifying and confirming the most suitable substitute when the requested product is unavailable. 

Now, with this release, using the new product interchangeability master data model, aATP can determine the best alternative product for sales document requirements, supporting one-to-one, one-to-many, and one-to-zero supersession chains, as well as FFF classes. The solution applies location-specific or cross-location substitution rules and configurable sequencing during availability checks, ensuring consistent and efficient product substitution decisions.

Business benefits:

  • Ensure uninterrupted customer fulfillment through automated product substitutions during product phase-ins, phase-outs, and supply transitions.

  • Improve planning and execution alignment with a single, consistent product interchangeability model used across planning, aATP, and fulfillment processes.
  • Increase order fulfillment rates and reduce delays by proactively leveraging interchangeable products to meet customer demand.

Event-driven backorder processing with new ACR framework

When a business event changes the supply-demand situation, such as a goods receipt for a specific material or plant, order confirmations need to be re-evaluated based on the updated availability picture. 
 
The new Availability Change Response (ACR) framework enables event-driven Backorder Processing (BOP), allowing planners to automatically reassess impacted orders following relevant supply changes. BOP runs can leverage predefined segments or manually maintained order due lists, focusing on backorders affected by the newly available material.

Business benefits:

  • Improve customer service levels by responding quickly to supply changes and updating order confirmations accordingly.

  • Increase fulfillment efficiency by focusing backorder processing on orders impacted by the changed availability situation.
  • Reduce manual effort and planning delays through automated, event-driven re-evaluation of customer commitments.

Prioritize critical customer demands with Order Due Lists

Order Due Lists (ODLs) enable planners to create and maintain prioritized lists of high-value sales orders and stock transport orders that require special consideration during Backorder Processing (BOP). 
Requirements can be added manually, through predefined selections, Excel uploads, or BOP segments, allowing businesses to align fulfillment decisions with operational and customer priorities. By combining ODLs with BOP variants, planners can supplement automated prioritization rules with business-critical exceptions and strategic commitments.

Business benefits:

  • Protect key customer commitments by prioritizing critical orders during backorder processing.

  • Enable faster response to changing business priorities through easy maintenance of prioritized order lists.
  • Give planners greater control over scarce supply allocation while maintaining a scalable backorder processing approach.

Alternative-Based Confirmations (ABC) in Interactive backorder processing (iBOP)

Interactive Backorder Processing (BOP) now supports requirements with alternative-based confirmations, enabling planners to review and adjust substituted product confirmations more effectively. 
Planners can manually modify confirmation dates and quantities for individual subitems, evaluate multiple requirements simultaneously, and leverage delivery proposals to accelerate decision-making. 
In addition, a new OData API enables mass updates of confirmations for sales documents and stock transport orders from external systems, supporting seamless integration across enterprise processes.
 

Business benefits:

  • Increase order fulfillment rates by enabling efficient review and adjustment of confirmations involving substituted products.

  • Streamline integration and automation with API-based mass updates of confirmations from external planning and execution systems.
 

Increase Order Confirmation Reliability with Stock Hiding and Stock Projection

Stock Hiding and Stock Projection help ensure that customer orders are confirmed only against inventory that is truly ready for fulfillment. 
 
Stock that has physically arrived but is still undergoing putaway, quality inspection, or other warehouse processes can remain hidden from availability checks, preventing premature commitments. 
At the same time, stock projection provides early visibility of this incoming inventory in its target location within the ATP time series, enabling planners to anticipate future availability and make better-informed decisions.
 

Business benefits:

  • Increase order confirmation reliability by preventing commitments against stock that is not yet available for picking or shipment.

  • Reduce fulfillment risks and customer disappointments caused by premature allocation of incoming inventory.
  • Improve planning accuracy with earlier visibility into incoming supply and its expected availability.
 

Improve Planning Accuracy for Length-Based Products

Built on Characteristics-Dependent Planning (CDP) in PP/DS, length-based availability checks enable precise planning and confirmation of products such as cables, where availability depends not only on total quantity but also on individual cut lengths and piece requirements.
 
With this release, length-based and characteristics-based evaluations can also be executed during Backorder Processing (BOP) and across additional document types, including sales orders, stock transport orders, orders without charge, and PP/DS production and planned orders.

Business benefits:

  • Increase fulfillment reliability for cable and other length-based products by ensuring customer commitments can be met with available inventory and supply.
  • Reduce manual intervention and planning complexity through automated length-based availability checks across planning and order fulfilment processes.
  • Extend consistent planning logic across the supply chain with support for additional document types and backorder processing scenarios.

Supply Protection Enhancements

This release introduces several enhancements to Supply Protection, improving flexibility, accuracy, and transparency in supply allocation and protection processes:

  • MRP Area Support: Supply protection can now be configured at the plant/MRP area level, enabling more granular and targeted protection without affecting other MRP areas within the same plant.
  • Improved Handling of Partial Deliveries: Only quantities that have not yet been delivered are reassigned, while partially delivered quantities retain their original supply protection assignment.
  • Refined Check Horizon Logic: Protected quantities beyond the check horizon are no longer considered during availability checks, helping prevent unintended restrictions from supply protections maintained far into the future.
  • Enhanced API Capabilities: The Supply Availability Protection Plan API (API_SUPAVAILYPROTPLAN_G4BA) now supports access to protection group consumption data, providing greater visibility and integration opportunities for monitoring and analytics

Business Benefits:

  • More precise supply allocation through granular MRP area-level protection.
  • Improved fulfillment accuracy by preserving supply assignments for partial deliveries.
  • Better order confirmations by preventing unnecessary restrictions from future-dated protections.
  • Increased visibility and integration through API access to protection consumption data.
  • Higher customer service levels through more effective management of constrained supply.

Functionality and Usability Improvements

This release introduces a range of enhancements that simplify administration, improve usability, and provide greater flexibility in configuring and executing aATP processes:

  • Expanded aATP Characteristic Catalogs: Nondocument fields, including process status and check-derived attributes such as source of supply in TPOP scenarios and product allocation sequences, can now be added to characteristic catalogs. Custom fields are also supported through BAdI extensions.

  • Enhanced Checking Rule Determination: Availability check rules can now be configured based on additional criteria, including order type, location, and item category, enabling more tailored availability check behavior.

  • Full-Quantity Product Allocation: A new allocation option ensures that only the full requested quantity is consumed from an allocation period. If sufficient quantity is unavailable, no allocation is consumed, preventing partial confirmations.

  • Confirmation-Based BOP Prioritization: Backorder Processing (BOP) and Interactive BOP now support the selection and prioritization of sales orders and stock transport orders based on their current confirmation status.

  • Simplified Bulk Maintenance: New copy-and-paste functionality, including Microsoft Excel integration, along with select-all and delete options, significantly accelerates the maintenance of large volumes of selection conditions in applications such as Configure BOP Segment and Manage Confirmations for Backorders.

  • Availability Info API Enhancement: The new DetermineCheckHorizon service operation enables users to determine the check horizon date at the MRP-area level, simplifying validation and troubleshooting of availability check settings.

  • Improved Product Allocation Reuse: When a sales order references another sales order, existing product allocation consumptions from the referenced order can now be reused, ensuring greater consistency and more efficient allocation management.

Business Benefits

  • Greater flexibility and control through more configurable availability checks, product allocation, and backorder processing.
  • Reduced administrative effort with bulk maintenance capabilities and streamlined condition management.
  • Improved order fulfillment accuracy by enabling full-quantity allocation rules and confirmation-based prioritization.
  • Enhanced visibility and decision-making through expanded characteristic catalog options and improved API support.
  • Faster integration and troubleshooting with easier access to check horizon and allocation consumption information.

Conclusion

These enhancements represent the key innovations delivered in SAP Advanced Available-to-Promise (aATP) as part of the October 2026 (2025 FPS02) release of SAP Cloud ERP, Private Edition, further strengthening order fulfillment, supply allocation, visibility, and usability capabilities across the order-to-cash process.

Looking ahead, SAP remains committed to advancing the next generation of order promising solutions, leveraging AI-powered assistance, intelligent automation, and AI agents to help organizations make faster, more informed fulfillment decisions, improve operational efficiency, and deliver more reliable customer commitments in increasingly dynamic supply chain environments.

entry.title: From External Service to Field Execution: Crowd Workforce Integration in SAP S/4HANA and SAP FSA
entry.content:
Crowd Integration Between S/4HANA and FSA

Business Context

If your organisation uses SAP S/4HANA for service management and SAP Field Service and Asset (FSA) for field execution, you've likely hit this wall: your external contractors exist in both systems, but those systems have never talked to each other about them. Every external service item in a service scenario required someone to manually create a matching activity in FSA. Every purchase order got created by a procurement person acting on an email. Every timesheet required a manual service confirmation entry in S/4HANA. On the FSA side, the dispatcher had no visibility of the lean service order at all. Every external service item requires someone to manually create a matching activity in FSA, attach the right reference, and keep it in sync with S/4HANA. The lean service process and the field execution process ran in parallel — connected only by people making phone calls and sending emails between them. The integration was you.

As of the 2025 FPS02 release, that changes. The Crowd Workforce Integration is now a standard feature of the S/4HANA–FSA product landscape, delivered through the existing standard Cloud Integration package. It keeps the master data in sync automatically — suppliers and their technicians replicate from S/4HANA to FSA as Crowd Partners and Technicians without any manual intervention. And it wires the lean service procurement chain directly to FSA crowd workforce events — so the PO is created when the supplier accepts the work, the SES is created when the technician logs their time, and the confirmation follows automatically. This post explains what problem it solves, what it delivers, and how it works end to end.

Blog Series:

Part 1: Crowd Integration Between S/4HANA and FSA -- Business Context, Solution Architecture, How it Works

Part 2: Make It Work: Configuring Crowd Integration Across S/4HANA and FSA

The Problem in Plain Terms

Field service operations that rely on external contractors — subcontractors, specialist partners, crowd workforce networks — sit at the intersection of two SAP platforms. S/4HANA owns the service order, the procurement chain, and the financials. FSA owns the dispatching, the Partner Portal, and the mobile execution. Before this integration, the two systems simply didn't know what each other was doing with the external workforce.

Here are the five gaps that teams were bridging manually every day:

Duplicate master data with no sync Suppliers and their technicians (Service Performers) lived in S/4HANA. The same people — modelled as crowd partners and technicians in FSA — had to be maintained separately in FSA. No link. No sync. When a new technician joined a supplier, someone updated S/4HANA and then manually created the same person in FSA. When someone left, both systems needed updating independently.

External service items invisible to FSA dispatchers When a service manager created a service order with an external service item (SREW/SRVW), FSA saw nothing. A dispatcher couldn't assign it because it didn't exist in their system. Someone had to manually create an FSA activity, attach the right reference, and keep it in sync with the S/4HANA item. With any volume of external work, this became a daily overhead.

No feedback from FSA back into S/4HANA Who accepted the assignment? When did field execution start? Which technician actually did the work? S/4HANA had no answers to these questions because FSA had no way to push that information back. The service order item sat with no visibility of its real-world status until someone manually updated it.

Purchase orders created by hand at the wrong time The lean service procurement chain — Purchase Requisition, Purchase Order, Service Entry Sheet, Service Confirmation — is a financial control process. The PO should be created when a supplier actually commits to doing the work, not before and not days after. Without integration, POs were created manually based on phone calls or emails, often at the wrong moment, and with no automated link to the underlying activity.

Timesheets disconnected from financial postings When a technician finished work and logged time in the FSA mobile app, that information had to travel by email or paper to a finance user who then manually created a service confirmation in S/4HANA. Month-end closings turned into reconciliation exercises. Errors were common. The gap between actual cost and recognised cost could span days or weeks.

 What the Integration Delivers

The integration closes all five gaps. Here's the direct outcome for each:

Gap

Solution

Duplicate master data

Supplier BPs and service performers in S/4HANA replicate automatically to FSA as Crowd Partners and Technicians. Incremental changes sync — new technicians added, deactivated technicians inactivated.

External items invisible to FSA

On service order release, the external service item is automatically created in FSA as an activity with subtype 'External Item' and a full reference back to the S/4HANA documents.

No FSA-to-S/4HANA feedback

Assignment acceptance and activity release events push status and parties (vendor, service performer) back into the S/4HANA service order automatically.

Manual PO creation

The Purchase Order is created automatically when the crowd partner releases the activity for execution — zero manual intervention via the FSMIMPORT technical user.

Manual service confirmation

Time effort approval in FSA triggers automatic Service Entry Sheet creation and approval in S/4HANA, which triggers the Service Confirmation. Real-time cost capture.

 

How It Works: Master Data

The master data half of the integration is straightforward: it maps S/4HANA business partner structures to FSA crowd workforce structures. The key building block is the Supplier Business Partner with service performer relationships.

Crowd Workforce sync

In S/4HANA, a vendor who provides field service workers is modelled as a Business Partner with the Supplier (FLVN01) role. That supplier can have employees related to them through the BUR025 relationship type using partner function BBP005 — the Service Performer partner function, which becomes available when Business Function /SHCM/EE_BP_1 is activated. These employees are created with both Employee and Contingent Worker person types so that their Business Partner record carries both the Employee role and the Service Performer role.

When this structure is in place and the integration is active, the new Crowd Partner interface replicates it to FSA as follows:

S/4HANA Object

FSA Object

Business Partner — Supplier role (FLVN01)

Crowd Partner (company entity in FSA Crowd Workforce)

Employee BP with Service Performer role (on relationship with Supplier)

Crowd Admin/Technician

 Replication is event-driven and incremental. Adding a new service performer to a supplier creates a new Crowd Technician in FSA. Removing the relationship deactivates them. The customer doesn't need to touch FSA for any of this — S/4HANA is the single source of truth.

There's also a variant — where the supplier wants to manage their own technicians in FSA without replicating them from S/4HANA. In that case, only the Crowd Partner is created from the S/4HANA supplier. The technicians are added directly in FSA by the crowd partner admin. Part 2 of this series covers how to configure each variant.

How It Works: The Transaction Flow

Here's the complete end-to-end flow once master data is in place.

Service Transactional in conjunction with SAP FSA 

  1. S/4HANA — Service manager creates a service order in S/4HANA with one or more External Service Items (item category SRVW). These items represent work to be executed by an external supplier.
  2. S/4HANA — On Release — Service manager releases the service order. Two things happen automatically in parallel: S/4HANA creates a Purchase Requisition for the external service item (standard lean service procurement), and the CPI iFlow sends the service order and item to FSA.
  3. FSA —Service Call and an Activity for the external service item created. The activity carries subtype ‘External Service’ and an ExternalId in the format <ServiceOrder>/<Item>/<PurchaseRequisition>_<PRItem> — making the full procurement reference traceable directly from the FSA dispatching board.
  4. FSA — Dispatching Board — The FSA dispatcher opens the dispatching board, finds the new activity (filtered by service order or subtype 'External Service'), and assigns it to an available external resource (crowd resource) — one of the technicians replicated from the relevant supplier.
  5. FSA Partner Portal — S/4HANA update — Automatic — The crowd admin logs into the Crowd Partner Portal and accepts the assignment. On acceptance, the crowd.activity.accepted event is emitted and the Notify Service Order iFlow updates the S/4HANA service order with the Vendor Party as supplier. Once the Crowd admin assigns Activity to a technician the Service Performer will be populated as the assigned technician.
  6. FSA Partner Portal — The crowd admin releases the activity for field execution, this is the moment that triggers the crowd.activity.released business event to create a Purchase Order against the existing Purchase Requisition in S/4HANA. The service order item execution status changes to 'In Execution'. No manual procurement needed. For traceability, the Activity ExternalId is updated as <ServiceOrder>/<Item>/<PurchaseRequisition>_<PRItem>/<PurchaseOrder>_<POItem>
  7. FSA Mobile App — The technician executes the work and logs time effort in the FSA mobile app via the EMME (Efforts, Materials, Mileage, Expenses) journal.
  8. FSA Partner Portal or FSA TimeApprovals— The crowd admin reviews and approves the time effort in FSA.
  9. S/4HANA —On approval of the time effort, a Service Entry Sheet in S/4HANA referring to the Purchase Order created in step 6. The SES is automatically approved by the standard interface.
  10. S/4HANA — S/4HANA automatically creates a Service Confirmation on SES approval. Actual cost is recognised against the service order. No manual posting required.
  11. FSA/S/4HANA — Existing Process — Non-time EMME entries like materials, mileage & other expenses — follow the existing standard FSA service confirmation flow. No change to that path.

See It In Action

Here is the E2E demo video of automated service scenario between S/4HANA & FSA:

 

What Gets Created Automatically: The Document Chain

To make the automation concrete — here's every document that gets created without a human touching it, and the trigger for each:

Document

Created When

Created By

Purchase Requisition

Service Order Release

S/4HANA lean service procurement (standard)

FSA Service Call

Service Order Release

CPI: Replicate Service Order iFlow

Service Order Release

CPI: Replicate Service Order iFlow

Purchase Order

CPI: Route Payload iFlow → New Notify Crowd update interface

Service Entry Sheet

EMME time effort approved in FSA

CPI: Route Payload iFlow → New Service Entry Sheet interface

Service Confirmation

SES auto-approval

S/4HANA standard (on SES approval)

 The External Service item is updated with all other crowd business events like below:

FSM Crowd Business Event

Vendor Party updated & Executing Service Employee on the Ext. Service Item

crowd.activity.assigned

  Availability

The Crowd Workforce Integration is a standard, supported feature as of SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud 2025 FPS02. It does not require a separate connector licence or custom development — it extends the existing SAP S/4HANA to SAP FSA integration package delivered through SAP BTP Integration Suite. If you already have the standard S/4HANA–FSA integration running, you're building on the same infrastructure.

entry.title: Make It Work: Configuring Crowd Integration Across SAP S/4HANA and SAP FSA
entry.content:
This post is for the consultants and administrators who are actually setting up the Crowd Workforce Integration between SAP S/4HANA and SAP FSA. Part 1 of this series covered the business problem and how the integration works end to end. Here we get into the specifics: what to configure, in which system, in what order, and what to check when you're done.

Blog Series:

Part 1: Crowd Integration Between S/4HANA and FSA -- Business Context, Solution Architecture, How it Works

Part 2: Make It Work: Configuring Crowd Integration Across S/4HANA and FSA

We cover two deployment scenarios. Scenario A is the standard setup where technicians are replicated from S/4HANA service performers. Scenario B is the variant — used when the crowd partner wants to manage their own technicians directly in FSA without a corresponding employee record in S/4HANA.

Prerequisites at a Glance

System

Object / Setting

Action

Why It Matters

SAP S/4HANA

Business Function /SHCM/EE_BP_1

Activate in Switch Framework (transaction SFW5)

Enables the Service Performer partner function BBP005 and BUR025 relationship type for Business Partners while converting the Employee to Business Partner

SAP S/4HANA

SAP Note 0002882172

Review and apply as required

Documents known issues and corrections related to the /SHCM/EE_BP_1 Business Function activation

SAP S/4HANA

Item Category for External Service Item

SRVW (or SREW for returns) configured in service order customising

Identifies service order items as external — triggers PR creation and FSA activity with subtype 'External Service

SAP S/4HANA

Lean Service Procurement

Standard lean service integration between SM and MM configured

Required for automatic PR creation on service order release

SAP BTP / CPI

SAP S/4HANA–FSA integration package

Already deployed and active

Crowd integration extends the existing iFlows — it does not replace them

SAP FSA

Crowd Workforce module

Licensed and enabled in the FSA tenant

Required for Crowd Partner and Technician objects to exist in FSA

SAP FSA

Crowd Partner Portal

Enabled in FSA tenant configuration

External crowd partners need portal access for assignment acceptance and EMME approval

 Scenario A: Standard Setup — Technicians Replicated from S/4HANA

This is the default scenario. Everything flows from S/4HANA: the supplier, their workers, and all field activity assignments are traceable back to S/4HANA records. Use this when the customer wants S/4HANA as the single system of record for both the supplier relationship and the individual technicians.

Step 1 — Activate Business Function /SHCM/EE_BP_1

Go to transaction SFW5 in S/4HANA. Locate Business Function /SHCM/EE_BP_1 and activate it. This is a permanent, irreversible activation — confirm with the customer before proceeding. Once activated, it makes the following available:

  • Partner function BBP005 (Service Performer) for use in Business Partner relationships
  • Relationship type BUR025 (Employee — has Service Performer) between a person BP and a company BP
  • The person type 'Contingent Worker' on Employee BPs, which generates the Service Performer BP role on BP conversion

Important: Review SAP Note 0002882172 before activating. It covers known corrections for this Business Function that may apply to your release level.

If Customer uses Employee Group other than “9” for contingent worker than a BADi implementation is required. Reference blog: External Workforce in Employee Business Partner Data Model

 Use the synchronization reports (/SHCM/RH_SYNC_BUPA_EMPL_SINGLE or /SHCM/RH_SYNC_BUPA_FROM_EMPL), to sync created employees as Business Partner with role BUP003 and BBP005.

 Step 2 — Configure Partner Function BBP005 for Relationship Type BUR025

Create your supplier as a Business Partner (transaction FLVN01) with the relevant purchasing organisation and currency. Then link the service performers to this supplier using relationship type BUR025 — Has Service Performer.

That's the trigger. Once those relationships are saved, the new CPI iFlow — "Replicate Crowd Partner and Technician from SAP S/4HANA to SAP Field Service and Asset Management" — picks them up automatically and creates the Crowd Partner and Crowd Technicians in FSA. Adding or removing service performers later is handled the same way — the changes flow through to FSA Crowd Workforce without any manual intervention.

One thing that must be in place before replication runs: make sure a valid address dependent email is maintained on both the Supplier BP and each Employee BP. FSA requires an email address to create Crowd Partner and Technician records — it's how the platform sends onboarding notifications to the crowd partner. Missing emails will stop the replication.

If you don't want to maintain individual technicians in S/4HANA, there's a configuration option for that. Set the iFlow external parameter “CrowdPartner W/O Service Performer” to true. In this mode, the supplier replicates to FSA as a Crowd Partner with a placeholder technician carrying the supplier's details. The crowd partner admin then manages their own technicians directly in FSA. This is the right choice when the customer wants to keep their external workforce data out of S/4HANA entirely.

Role Mapping: Crowd Admin vs Crowd Technician: employees created with both Employee and Contingent Worker person types get both the Crowd Admins roles in FSA.

Step 3 — Configure Item Category for External Service Items

In Customizing path “SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Service -> Transactions -> Basic Settings -> Define Item Category Determination”, ensure the item category SRVW and SREW are configured and assigned to the relevant order type (SRVO) and item category group (SRVP or DIEN).

With this you can add External Service item categories to the Service Order.

In Customer path “SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Service -> Transactions  Settings for Service Transactions -> Integration -> Logistics Integration -> Enterprise Organizational Management -> Define Logistics Scenario for Procurement of Materials and Services”, for the Purchase Requisition to auto create on the External Service Item, add PREQ as logistic.

If you are using legacy org, then patch will “SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Service -> Transactions  Settings for Service Transactions -> Integration -> Logistics Integration -> Organizational Management(Legacy) -> Define Logistics Scenario for Procurement of Materials and Services”

Step 4 — Add Vendor and Service Performer Parties in Service

To update the Vendor and External technician to the External service item, maintain Vendor (0000019) and Service Performer (0000028) functions against Ext. Service Item (00000032) & Ext. Confirmation Service Item (00000033) categories in the Partner Function determination in Service.

Customizing path: “SAP Customizing Implementation Guide -> Service -> Basic Functions -> Partner Processing -> Define Partner Determination Procedure in Service”

Step 5: Authorization to access Purchase apps:

Make sure you have below roles to view purchase orders, requisition and service entry sheet

SAP_BR_EMPLOYEE_PROCUREMENT, SAP_BR_PURCHASER. SAP_BR_INTERNAL_SALES_REP

Step 6: Maintain Purchasing Info Record:

Maintain mapping of Purchase Org and Plant with the Service Material and Supplier in Purchasing Info Record (tcode ME11). This is required to create purchase order using purchase requisition.

Step 7 — Configure the CPI iFlows

In SAP BTP Integration Suite, open the standard package “SAP S/4HANA Integration with SAP Field Service and Assent Management”. The four iFlows relevant to crowd integration are:

  • Replicate Service Order from SAP S4HANA to SAP Field Service and Asset Management SOAP — sends service order and external service item to FSA on release. Configure “External Service Item Categories” as SRVW,SREW.
  • Notify External Service Order Item with Crowd Changes from SAP Field Service and Asset Management to SAP S4HANA – sends all crowd updates to external item.
  • Crowd Service Entry Sheet Creation from SAP Field Service and Asset Management to SAP S4HANA – creates Service Entry Sheet on activity confirmations on external activity.
  • Route Payload from SAP Field Service and Asset Management to SAP S/4HANA — handles all inbound FSA crowd events

Step 8 —FSA Connector Events for Crowd Business Events

The crowd business events mentioned below will be routed through the FSM Connector outbound event to initiate CPI endpoint. There is not configuration required, this will be taken care by standard in FSA.

Event

When It Fires

What It Triggers in S/4HANA

crowd.activity.assigned and accepted

Crowd partner accepts assignment in Partner Portal

Updates Vendor and Service Performer on S/4HANA service order item

crowd.activity.released

Crowd partner releases activity for field execution

Triggers automatic PO creation in S/4HANA via FSMIMPORT

crowd.activity.cancelled

Assignment cancelled by crowd partner

Updates service order status in S/4HANA

crowd.activity.unassigned

Activity unassigned from crowd resource

Clears assignment data from S/4HANA service order item

EMME time effort approved

activity.confirmed on external activity

Crowd admin approves time effort booking

Creates SES (for time effort) + auto-approves + triggers Service Confirmation in S/4HANA

Create Service Confirmations for other non-time EMME’s like Expenses, Mileages, & Material

 Step 9 — Enable the Crowd Workforce Module in FSA

In FSA, go to Admin → Company Settings and verify that the Crowd module is enabled.

For details, refer to Configure Single Tenant Crowd.

Scenario B - Technicians Managed Only in FSA

Some customers want to onboard their external suppliers as crowd partners in FSA but don't want to maintain individual technician records in S/4HANA. The supplier manages their own workforce directly in FSA.

To achieve this, follow below handling in the configurations:

In the CPI iFlow parameters, configure “CrowdPartner W/O Service Performer” parameter as true in below iflows

  • Replicate Business Partner
  • Replicate Crowd Partner and Technician from SAP S4HANA to SAP Field Service and Asset Management
  • Crowd Service Entry Sheet Creation from SAP Field Service and Asset Management to SAP S4HANA
  • Notify External Service Order Item with Crowd Changes from SAP Field Service and Asset Management to SAP S4HANA

 The effects of that single flag change:

  • The Supplier BP still replicates to FSA as a Crowd Partner — the company-level entity is created
  • No Crowd Technicians or Admins are created from S/4HANA service performer relationships
  • The crowd partner admin creates and manages their own technicians directly in FSA
  • When the crowd partner accepts and releases assignments, S/4HANA receives the status update (In Execution) but not the Executing Service Employee nor Service Performer.

 Note that email is maintained on the Supplier in this scenario as well.

Scenario Comparison

Capability

Scenario A — Standard

Scenario B — Without Technician S4HANA

Technician data in S/4HANA

Required (employee BPs with BUR025 relationship)

Not required

Crowd Technician creation

Automatic from S/4HANA service performer replication

Manual, directly in FSA by crowd partner admin

Technician identity in S/4HANA

Visible on service order Parties Involved

Not populated (status update only)

Executing Employee on Confirmation

Actual technician from FSA assignment

Fallback to service order creator

Best for

Customers who manage supplier workforce in S/4HANA and want full traceability

Customers who let suppliers self-manage their teams in FSA

 EMME Processing: Two Paths, One Clear Rule

When a technician books work through the FSA EMME journal, the integration handles different entry types differently. This is worth understanding explicitly because it affects what gets created in S/4HANA.

Path A: Time Efforts

Time effort entries — the hours a technician spent on the job — go through a specific path that uses the Purchase Order created earlier in the process:

  1. Technician logs time effort in FSA mobile app
  2. Crowd admin approves the time effort
  3. CPI iFlow creates a Service Entry Sheet in S/4HANA referencing the Purchase Order
  4. The SES is automatically approved by the integration
  5. S/4HANA creates a Service Confirmation on SES approval — actual cost is posted

The SES → Confirmation path is what makes this integration financially compliant. The Purchase Order acts as the financial commitment, the SES captures the actual delivery, and the Confirmation posts the cost. This is the standard three-way match for service procurement.

Path B: Materials, Mileage, and Expenses

Non-time EMME entries — materials used, mileage driven, expenses incurred — follow the existing standard FSA service confirmation flow. There is no change to this path. These entries do not go through the SES route and are not tied to the Purchase Order. They create service confirmations directly in S/4HANA through the same mechanism that was already in place before the crowd integration.

Worth Clarifying with Customers: If your customer uses material items heavily in their EMME journals, make sure they understand that only time efforts go through the SES path. Material-based costs are confirmed separately and are not linked to the crowd PO.

entry.title: Release Highlights 2025 FPS02 : PP/DS in SAP Cloud ERP, Private Edition
entry.content:
SAP Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling (PP/DS) plays a pivotal role in SAP Cloud ERP, Private Edition by bridging strategic supply chain planning and operational execution through synchronized, constraint-based planning. By coordinating demand, supply, and production resources in real time, it helps organizations optimize plan quality, improve responsiveness, and enhance supply chain performance.
 
The 2025 FPS02 release (October 2026) of SAP Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling (PP/DS) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Private Edition brings significant advances across AI, analytics, user experience, and supply chain integration. 

Here're some of the key highlights what our customers can use -

AI-Assisted Production Capacity Overload Resolution

Production planners often lose hours resolving capacity conflicts manually - juggling component availability, operation sequences, and finite resource constraints. With this release, PP/DS introduces its AI-assisted planning capability to resolve capacity overload situation. 

When a capacity overload is detected, the system proposes alternative planning options, accounting for multiple constraints simultaneously. Planners can evaluate and act on recommendations, rather than identifying every option independently. 

Business benefits:

  • Increase planning performance through faster resolution of capacity overload situations
  • Improve agility to respond to short-term events such as unplanned machine downtime
  • Reduced planning time and improved plan quality

Embedded interactive KPI monitor

Making sense of a production plan - while you're still building it - has traditionally required switching between tools and saving intermediate states. That changes with the embedded KPI monitor.

PP/DS now integrates SAP Analytics Cloud-based KPIs directly into the planning applications (Advanced Scheduling Board, Production Planning Table, and others). Planners see live micro-charts covering resource utilization, orders, operations, and pegging - all without leaving the session. Colour-coded thresholds make critical situations immediately visible. Drill-down via review booklets provides the detail needed to act.

Business benefits:

  • Increase planner productivity through immediate plan validation.
  • Optimize operational performance by selecting the best planning scenario based on measurable business outcomes.
  • Enhance delivery reliability through early detection and resolution of capacity bottlenecks and scheduling conflicts.

Harmonized product substitution

This release introduces the first version of product substitution in PP/DS based on the SAP advanced Available-to-Promise (aATP) product interchangeability master data model.

The new model supports linear supersession chains with and without use-up of existing stock. It also unlocks additional flexibility: one predecessor product can now have different successors across different plants, and interchangeability in storage location MRP areas is supported.

Business benefits:

  • Create a single source of truth for product substitution decisions across the business.

  • Increase operational efficiency through simplified master data governance and reduced maintenance overhead.
  • Enhance customer fulfillment performance with consistent substitution logic applied from demand planning to order execution.

Advanced Scheduling Board: Extensibility, Analytics, and Productivity

 

The Advanced Scheduling Board now combines deep extensibility with embedded analytics, enabling planners to make faster, more informed decisions without leaving their workflow. Custom buttons, BADI-triggered actions, and customer-specific fields can be integrated directly into the planning experience, while seamless navigation between the Gantt chart and KPI monitor improves planner productivity and reduces decision latency.
 
New Fiori-native worklist apps have been introduced for Monitor Requirements and Order Conversion that improve planner effectiveness with real-time visibility, AI-assisted guidance, and streamlined exception management, helping teams respond faster and improve operational performance.
 

Synchronized Planning with IBP and aATP

By enhancing integration across planning systems and execution processes, PP/DS enables more accurate simulations, stronger plan adherence, and greater end-to-end supply chain visibility.
 
Time-dependent stock synchronization for inactive planning versions enables PP/DS and SAP IBP to align inventory projections across simulation scenarios, allowing planners to evaluate what-if alternatives with greater confidence and make better-informed decisions before committing changes.
 
Enhanced Flexible Constraints simplify the management of planning constraints across complex production environments, helping planners respond more quickly to changing conditions while maintaining operational efficiency.
 
Length-based planning via aATP and Supply creation-Based Configuration (SBC) aligns customer commitments for right length products, improving planning accuracy, reducing fulfilment risk, and ensuring more reliable execution for length-based products, predominantly used by cable industries.

Business benefits:

  • Improve simulation accuracy and planning confidence through synchronized inventory visibility across active and inactive planning scenarios.

  • Increase planning responsiveness with simplified management of production constraints across the manufacturing network.
  • Enhance fulfilment reliability by aligning customer commitments with feasible production supply for length-based material

Advancements in Core Planning and Industry-Specific Capabilities

This release delivers targeted innovations that help manufacturers improve planning accuracy, increase operational efficiency, and make better decisions across both core and industry-specific planning processes.

Tank Planning - Improve asset utilization and reduce planning effort with more intelligent tank allocation that accounts for tank capacity as well as filling and draining requirements, resulting in more feasible and efficient production plans.

 
Flexible Constraints - Increase planner productivity and responsiveness with a simplified, more intuitive approach to managing production constraints across the entire operation.

 Production Planning Optimizer (PPO) - Create plans that better reflect business priorities through enhanced optimization controls, like support target quantities, configurable soft penalties for supply deviations, and priority-based constraint filtering, enabling more accurate supply planning, improved service levels, and better resource utilization.

 Extended Subcontracting Support - Gain a complete view of sourcing alternatives by planning in-house production, subcontracting, and external procurement - all together during the Production Planning Optimizer (PPO) run, helping reduce supply risks, improve decision-making, and optimize costs.

 Enhanced Shelf-Life Planning - Reduce waste and improve inventory accuracy with better visibility into expiring stock and surplus quantities, ensuring planning decisions are based on a realistic view of available inventory with acceptable shelf-life parameters.

Business benefits:

  • Accelerate planning cycles through a flexible and adaptable scheduling environment.

  • Enable data-driven decisions with embedded performance insights and AI-powered assistance.
  • Streamline planner workflows by reducing context switching and consolidating key planning activities in one workspace.

Conclusion

The 2025 FPS02 release of SAP PP/DS represents a significant step forward in making production planning more intelligent, connected, and user-centric. From the introduction of the first AI-assisted planning agent and embedded analytics to harmonized product substitution, advanced scheduling innovations, and deeper integration with SAP IBP and aATP, the release empowers planners to make faster, more informed decisions while improving plan quality and execution reliability.

These innovations strengthen PP/DS's role as a critical component of synchronized supply chain planning, helping organizations better align demand, supply, capacity, and production constraints in real time. By combining AI-driven assistance, enhanced visibility, simplified planning processes, and industry-specific capabilities, SAP continues to help manufacturers improve agility, optimize resource utilization, and deliver more reliable customer commitments across increasingly complex supply chains.

Looking ahead, SAP remains committed to advancing the future of production planning and scheduling through continued investments in AI, analytics, and end-to-end supply chain integration, enabling planners to move from reactive decision-making to intelligent, proactive orchestration of manufacturing operations.
